speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head T of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: As a Member of the Class of 2011 in Parliament, like me, many Members of this House would have personally experienced the volume of appeals by our residents regarding housing matters from 2009 through to 2013.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many were young couples, and even their parents who came to Meet-the-People Sessions were anxious and perhaps also perplexed by the housing situation then.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Many try and try but were constantly unsuccessful in their applications for a flat.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Fast forward to today, we can mostly agree that the situation has gotten much better.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Just by volume of cases, you can tell that the increase in supply and the multiple improvements that have been made and introduced by then Minister Khaw Boon Wan and, more recently, by Minister Lawrence Wong and the Ministry of National Development (MND) team have made a difference.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This is a Ministry that has listened intently to feedback from the public and suggestions from backbenchers for a re-emphasis on the centrality of housing to the social compact that we have with fellow Singaporeans, and that there are housing options for Singaporeans at every life-stage.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While the appeals on purchased flats have dropped, there is still work required on the other end of the housing spectrum, and this is rental housing.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: At last year's Committee of Supply (COS), I spoke on the issue of co-living, as well as our public rental flat schemes.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am thankful that the Ministry has made improvements on many fronts, yet it is still an issue that vexes.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I, therefore, welcome the Senior Parliamentary Secretary's reiteration yesterday that public rental should be temporary.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: To help households in rental housing to move to home ownership is certainly not straightforward.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: There are multiple issues that rental families face.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Yet, with a scheme that has been in place since December 2016, the numbers seem to indicate a fresh but not so fast start.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I took a look at the available numbers.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And 3,500 households across 56,000 rental units seem to indicate that the journey, though encouraged, is honestly quite fraught.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Most of us would have rental households in our constituencies.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We are certainly proud and happy for our residents who have successfully progressed to purchasing their own homes.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: But do we also shed a tear for the many who are left behind?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have seen their struggles first-hand trying to hold a job, fight ill health, balance family needs, pay debts and, for some of them, stay on the straight and narrow.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For us and many community partners, we do whatever we can to help them.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Yet, often, challenges remain and continue to surface that keep them from completely lifting themselves up.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I am, therefore, heartened by the Senior Parliamentary Secretary's announcement of a Home Ownership Support team to provide stronger personalised help for those with potential for home ownership.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The work for the new team will certainly not be easy.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could the Ministry, therefore, update the House on the ambit of this new team and what are the conditions that the team will be looking at to identify households that can potentially become home owners?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Based on the understanding of these criteria, could I also ask the Ministry how many rental households today would potentially move towards home ownership in the next five years and what are the main barriers that would keep the rest from moving towards these aspirations?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While we address the issue of families progressing to home ownership from rental, there is also a group which faces even greater challenges.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: These are our elderly poor, often single, without family support.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Last year, I raised the issue of joint-singles where co-tenants are unable to get along.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Would the Ministry consider having more rental flats refurbished to provide for more privacy within the flats for co-tenants to have some semblance of their own space?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Also, I would suggest for an adjustment period to be included for the benefit of both co-tenants so that they have time to adjust to each other before committing to a full rental contract.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This could be for a month and come with certain preconditions.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: From elders in rental flats to elderly home owners, the Ministry has provided additional options over the years.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One example is the Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS).

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: After the enhanced LBS was first announced by Deputy Prime Minister Tharman Shanmugaratnam in 2012, fellow Members and I have pushed for greater adoption of the scheme and also for the scheme to be extended.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have actively promoted LBS to my older residents and, as I have a high number of larger flats, the extension is welcome news for my residents.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, I also wish to point out that there are many who are still unaware of the details and grapple with issues surrounding leaving an asset for their children or should they live beyond the period under the LBS agreement.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Would the Ministry, therefore, consider better communication on the scheme and perhaps offer a customised info-kit to home owners who qualify for the scheme so that they can be better informed of their options?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Related to this is, of course, diminishing lease and its impact on home prices.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I would also point out that while this will open up the market for older flats and allow younger home owners the option of purchasing an older flat using more of their CPF, we must not solve two problems and yet move the main issue of diminishing leases further down the line.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For younger aspiring home owners as well as second-timers, the Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) Scheme and the Re-Offer of Balance Flat (ROF) Scheme are often seen as the easier and quicker option to getting keys to your own flat.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could the Ministry also clarify how the first-come-first-served system will be fair for all?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If the ROF scheme under the new arrangement is proven to be a successful model, I would ask that the Ministry also consider extending it to the SBF scheme as well.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Over the years, I have also been making an appeal for better access to housing for singles and single parents.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have made big strides for singles and the extension of grants in the last two years have been helpful for many applicants.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, one feedback I have consistently received is that while the grants are attractive, often they are hard to qualify for, such as the proximity grant when the estates that singles wish to apply for close to their parents or child are of larger flat types that they do not qualify for.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: However, the requirement for approval of the former spouse to purchase a flat often still serves as a major barrier.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could the Ministry, therefore, consider further relaxing this requirement?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Mr Chairman, we live in a fast-changing world.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Singapore prides itself as a city that keeps pace with technology.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Could the Ministry update on the plans to make our nation's built infrastructure future-ready?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In doing so, can we also ensure that it continues to be a welcoming and liveable city where all Singaporeans can feel a part of?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What are the challenges that lie ahead of us?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Last year, I had the privilege of accompanying President Halimah on her State Visit to the Netherlands.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: While there, I saw for myself the Dutch living out the Polder Culture in all aspects of their lives, especially in how they build and plan their city.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Like us, we are a small country surrounded by water and at risk of global warming and rising sea levels.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I watched a simulation there at the Research Institute of our city centre flooded as seawaters rise.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The reality is that the risks are real.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How can we plan in advance for this possibility and learn from the experiences of others?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It must be one that is endearing and enduring.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Our homes must be places of comfort and safety, our communities built on trust and cohesiveness, our environment green and welcoming, our nation united and strong.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: At the root of it all is our compact with Singaporeans, a promise that we have kept and must continue to keep – come hell or high water.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Indeed, we are constantly building up, expanding out and tunneling down.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: As we develop and transform our city, how will the Ministry continue to ensure that housing, industry and business needs are met as we stay green, create space for agricultural development and take measures against the effects of global warming?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Housing and Development Board (HDB) flats will continue to be where the majority of Singaporeans make their home.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The benefit of a "whole-of-precinct" or even "whole-of-estate" redevelopment project is a better integrated layout with improved accessibility and connectivity.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Infrastructure could also be improved in a more holistic manner.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Another plus is the viability of installing systems incorporating new technologies, such as the pneumatic waste conveyance system.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Redeveloping a precinct or a cluster of precincts may even be more economical and technically easier to carry out.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: HDB is not only the main provider of housing.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It also has to fulfill many social objectives.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: HDB estates must foster inclusivity through the distribution of household types as well as the design and layout of high-quality social and community facilities.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Meeting the needs of different family compositions, the elderly, persons with special needs and other vulnerable groups require redesigning blocks, the precincts and surrounding facilities.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is far more feasible to have a total makeover than piecemeal renewal.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would the Minister share with us an update on the major projects to make Singapore more resilient in the face of climate change?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will our city be sufficiently equipped to deal with or, better still, lead other cities, in technological advances?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: To attract more investments, we need good infrastructure and buildings which provide reliable and seamless support to businesses and industries, particularly those in the innovative and cutting-edge sectors.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Whether we are building homes, tunnels or roads, we must constantly check and enforce the high quality of our structures through construction oversight and strict audits of certification works.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What measures does MND have in place to enhance the quality and safety of our building projects?

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should be a city which is not only efficient and functional, but also beautiful and interesting, with buildings reflecting our unique historical and cultural heritage.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We should be a city attractive to visitors but, more importantly, a joy to live and work in for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In this aspect, I urge the Ministry to continue to provide support to HDB to create beautiful and practical homes and estates.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We want to become more independent in terms of our food supply.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This is a great challenge in our land-scarce island.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Would the Ministry share its plans for helping our farming communities through the creation of space and building of supporting infrastructure?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: This time round, more so than for previous years, there will be intense public interest to see how URA will lay out its vision for the physical future of our country.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I can also sense palpable excitement on the ground, with some calling this the Master Plan for underground space.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is quite cliched to talk about how technology is changing our lives, but they are definitely new developments that could fundamentally change how we think about physical space.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: For example, the advent of autonomous vehicles (AVs) could totally revolutionise land use.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: One direct but profound outcome is less need for parking in each building, as fewer people will drive themselves.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Commuters will arrive in AVs, which will then drive off and pick up other passengers.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: It is not uncommon now to have three to five storeys of every building dedicated to carparks.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Another issue of concern is the potential impact of climate change, such as rising sea levels.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: A Master Plan typically has a 10- to 15-year planning horizon, but buildings can easily last 30 to 40 years.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How do we balance the long- and short-term needs and make optimal use of scarce land?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: At the same time, we need to balance commercial uses with recreational space and maintain greenery even within the central core.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I would, therefore, like to ask the Minister how the URA will ensure that the Master Plan will effectively support our next phase of growth.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How will this be done and what can the public expect to see?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have noticed significant rejuvenation within the CBD over the last few years, as old buildings have been replaced or refurbished to meet future needs.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Trends, such as the rise of co-working, have also helped to bring more vibrancy into the CBD, as smaller companies and startups can now afford space downtown.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: How does MND plan to also rejuvenate older areas of the city, within the CBD, as well as in the surrounding areas?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The Government shared plans about the Greater Southern Waterfront (GSW) last year.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The opportunity to replace the existing port operations at Tanjong Pagar is exciting, given the prime location so close to both the CBD and to leisure zones, such as Sentosa.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What can we expect to see at the GSW and what is the timeline for realising these plans?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh, you have five minutes for your three cuts.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is really not conducive for family planning.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Most of these couples put up at their parents’ flats instead of renting in the interim to save money for their future.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Considering that current flats are not big, it is quite a squeeze to house another new family member with babies on the way.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Because of this, most couples postpone having a child until they get their own flats, which is again not ideal, as more and more couples are getting married when they are older, in their 30s.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hence, it would be really helpful if the wait can be shortened.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: After all, the more children there are, the greater the urgency for more space.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will also encourage our young couples to have more children as they can be assured that they do not have to wait too long when they need to upgrade to bigger flats to house more kids.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Lastly, will the Ministry consider additional measures to encourage first-timers to continue to live near their parents in existing mature estates?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Can some form of additional rebates or incentives be provided?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This is because first-timer young couples have to pay a premium for these locations, which are generally more centralised and have more amenities.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: What measures will MND take to ensure mature estates remain vibrant and liveable, especially with the falling average household size?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How about building more BTO flats targeted at young families?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: This will enable young couples to stay near their parents, and their children will bring more vibrancy to a mature area with high numbers of the elderly.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: To optimise our car parks, would HDB and URA consider introducing another type of season parking, namely, for half a day, either day or night parking, at HDB, URA and heavy vehicle car parks to provide an alternative for those who do shift work and to ease their parking needs and optimise the parking space?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, the release of each BTO estate brings about better upgrades and facilities than the last one, reflecting the needs of the different demographics over the years.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: From the early days of no-frills living to the addition of playgrounds and fitness amenities, to green-living aesthetics, HDB flats have come a long way.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Yet, this creates a significant difference between the mature estates and newer estates, and there are some concerns that mature estates will not catch up with the newer estates in terms of technology and liveability.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Imagine living in a non-smart technology enabled estate and then visiting a grandchild's new estate and finding it too foreign to navigate.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The state and appearance of one's living environment projects a certain standard of living, so we do not want to create a situation whereby residents living in different neighbourhood estates have a different quality of life.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Moreover, estates should be upgraded regularly to maintain safety and inject freshness in the neighbourhood.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: What is the Ministry doing to ensure HDB estates and flats remain liveable and vibrant even as they age?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Ministry share how the timeline is decided for the implementation of upgrading projects in the older mature estates, so that they can catch up with the newer estates?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will rental flats benefit from these upgrades as well?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Their flats would require repair in many areas.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Despite the conditions of these flats, many residents are waiting and hoping.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: They want to save on renovation cost because many are elderly, retired or semi-retired.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In private estates, many residents look forward to the Estate Upgrading Programme (EUP).

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Like HDB estates, amenities around the private estates, too, deteriorate with the years, and they too should be subject to renewal.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We can serve the private estates better by introducing more community facilities, like playing fields, courts, carparks and so on, and create opportunities for the neighbours to come together to facilitate community togetherness.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Designated Smoking Points (DSPs) are increasingly popular among my residents.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We have been relying on private funds to build the DSPs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can we tap into the Community Improvement Projects Committee (CIPC) funding for maintenance and addition of new DSPs?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: With CIPC funding, more DSPs can be rolled out to other parts of Singapore, too.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Perhaps, HDB should be bold enough to pilot smoke-free new BTO blocks.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Buyers are informed upfront that there is no smoking allowed in the block, including their own homes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have residents who have been asking to sell their flats before the five-year minimum occupation period (MOP) is up as they cannot stand the smoke from their neighbours.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Next, my residents who use heavy vehicles for work often face a long wait for heavy vehicle parking in Yishun Town.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many new residents who shifted into new BTOs are having difficulty in buying season parking.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many have to wake up early and stop work till very late.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, they take the risk of parking along the service road near their homes and ended up receiving summonses regularly.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have made such requests many times in Parliament.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Although divorcees with care and control of children can now buy subsidised flats without the three-year restriction, when the ex-spouse is not cooperative, it becomes difficult to sell their matrimonial homes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, they do not have money to buy their next flat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope more can be done to facilitate the post-divorce sale of flat process.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have been asking for an AXS machine to be installed at Block 507 where there are coffee shops and other shops.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I was told that HDB is charging $200 per month.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Hence, the operating cost of an AXS machine is $500 to $600 per month.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can HDB waive the fee so that the service providers are more willing to provide such essential services?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope MND can address all the above for our endearing homes.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The more we do, the more enduring our homes are.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Mr Chairman, in our HDB estates, our void decks are anything but empty.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: They can be places of friendship and fellowship, when neighbours gather.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The void deck can be a place of joy, a wedding venue for a community to celebrate.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The void deck can be a place of sadness when a resident has passed away and family, friends and neighbours come to say goodbye.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The void deck can be a place of potential, a white space that can someday be used for a social service office (SSO), a senior activity centre (SAC), a kindergarten and more.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But some residents worry about the shape of newer HDB blocks that do not have void decks.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some of my older residents may someday move in with their children.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Some may be affected by Selective En Bloc Redevelopment Scheme (SERS) and move from old blocks to new blocks within Clementi.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: My older residents look upon newer precincts with some curiosity.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: The see the new pavilions, the new sky gardens.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: But, to these seniors, they feel it is quite different from the void decks.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Maybe not so adaptable, not so airy, something different.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: However, residents there were reported to be suffering from growing pains as the infrastructure and services in the estate did not keep up with the growing population.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Residents found themselves staring at growing congestion and longer commuting time with each new development sprouting up in the estate.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: In another report, it was stated that the traffic congestion in Punggol has been a long-standing problem, stretching back to almost five years ago.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Even when a new link road connecting Punggol Centre to the nearby expressways came into operation, one resident predicted that the traffic congestion would return in a few years' time.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Amenities like childcare centres, healthcare facilities, and food outlets were also reported to be in need of improvement to meet the demands of the growing population in Punggol.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: There are now new housing estates and condominiums sprouting up and the traffic on Hougang Avenue 7 enroute to KPE is also coming to a crawl every weekday morning.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: This part of the estate is also short on amenities like childcare centres.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Residents in Hougang can already predict what is to come in the not-too-distant future when more people start to move into the new developments in the estate.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Would we be seeing a repeat of what the residents of Punggol were experiencing the past five years?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Would other upcoming estates be facing the same problems as well?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Some things can be hard to predict but we are living in an era of big data.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat (Hougang)
text: Some trends and problems can be predicted and anticipated with a fair amount of accuracy.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Manap, you can take both your cuts.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The common presenting issue is that they are unable to find a parking lot for heavy vehicles, resulting in them parking their vehicles illegally.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Many of them were issued fines while they were attending to their needs, such as answering to nature's call and when buying packed food for lunch or dinner during their working hours.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The fines imposed have a great impact on them financially.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: This dual parking lots have double markings, one marking with the dimension to cater for Class 3 vehicles while the second marking of a bigger dimension is for heavy vehicles.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Such dual parking lots will allow any type of vehicle to park on a first-come-first serve basis.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Such implementation will definitely facilitate heavy vehicle drivers to park legally when fulfilling their needs.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I do not have the information on when the last review was done.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: However, I do believe that it has been a while since it was conducted.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I do hope HDB will make this timely review.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: My experience visiting these flats are that many of the older rental flats face one another via a common corridor and there is little ventilation or light between the flats.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As a result, the entire area smelt musty and the living environment is usually not pleasant due to the presence of hoarded items.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: When I became a Member of Parliament for Mountbatten and visited the Dakota Crescent rental flats in the constituency, the living environment was much better as the flats were spacious and better ventilated.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, the building was almost 60 years old and one can see the wear and tear on the building and the facilities.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The lifts were old and break down regularly due to their age and the lack of spare parts.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: These lifts could not be upgraded due to the smaller size of the lift shaft and any extra lift extension could not serve every floor because of the design of the building.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Older rental flats usually result in hoarding by long-time residents and the collected items would be placed at the common corridor.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: As an example, the new rental flats at Cassia Crescent are better ventilated with more facilities in the building so that the residents can gather together outside their flats.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: The lift also stops at every floor and this allows elderly residents or those on wheelchairs to travel out of their flat.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I was glad to hear Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling speak yesterday about the setting up of the social service hub to offer services to the elderly.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: This is important because some of the elderly who are illiterate need help to understand official letters from Government agencies like HDB or the Town Council.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: They need help to understand their SP Services bills and even Police warnings about conmen cheating the elderly.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: So, the SSOs would be of great help to help these elderly illiterate residents understand messages better.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I also urge MND to consider providing more facilities to support the elderly residents in the rental block of flats.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Even simple things like having food stalls near the flats, bus stops near the rental flats would make life better for some of the elderly staying in the rental flats.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I was also delighted to hear of HDB's plans to help rental flat families own their own homes.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: For example, some of the residents at the rental flats at Dakota were offered the opportunity to buy their flat at Cassia Crescent.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: However, they did not take up the offer as they were concerned about buying a flat in a new and unfamiliar environment.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Having stayed there for a while, they found that the flat is suitable for their needs and wish to buy over the rental flat.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Public housing is one of the pillars of what it means to be a Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: But it is also one of our most under-appreciated forms of welfare.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Home ownership is a way for us to provide peace of mind, to give the lower-income a disproportionately higher amount from our national budget, and also to communicate important values, such as family togetherness, resilience and optimism about the future.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: We do so with a complicated jigsaw of home proximity grants, means testing and eligibility criteria to ensure that the most disadvantaged benefit the most.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Human lives are complex, and our rules reflect this complexity.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: Over the years, the rulebook for the sale, purchase and rental of HDB flats has become very thick indeed.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: One of the most important areas where I think Officer X can be deployed is to help the lower-income in rental flats.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: They also need to be able to help these families who want to move out from the flexi-flats and into bigger ones, including bending the rules on the MOP of 20 years.

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: (b) How does MND help public rental tenants to eventually own their own homes?

speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
text: (c) How can MND help to ensure rents remain affordable and do not disincentivise progress among tenants?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: From my observations, the public rental flat occupiers are mainly the single parents with children, seniors with no extended family, families with foreign spouse, families with interim issues and singles as co-tenants.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The first area, enhance guidance on the home ownership process.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: We should consider a few aspects that will be helpful for the families which had low income for an extended period.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: First, to provide more financial planning and more detailed assistance in guiding them on their first purchase so that they can make more informed decisions of flats that are within their buying power.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The second area, review rental rate based on more factors beyond household income.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Rental rate review today takes into account all household income of the occupiers in the flat.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: I feel that this needs to be reviewed more holistically or taken into account with a different treatment for each condition.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: For example, families that have once-off bonus, jobs that are commissioned based, odd jobs on project basis, families with sons who are serving National Service; these incomes cannot be treated in the same manner as a regular full-time source of income.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: Moving forward, if we want to enable social mobility for them, we need to look at the efforts of these families in stepping up and over different periods of their lifecycle.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The third area, invest in upkeeping of public rental flats.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: As we try to integrate public rental flats with regular flats in the newer housing estates, I would like to ask MND to also consider investing in upkeeping older rental flats.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: The exterior facades are now refreshed through the regular Town Council Maintenance Repair and Redecoration programmes.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (Fengshan)
text: However, there are many seniors living in these rental flats who are not only unable to afford interior renovation of their units, they are most likely going to live there for good as they have no next-of-kin.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Png, you have eight minutes for your three cuts.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I have a resident who has just made his sixth attempt to apply for a flat recently, having started the application process about two years ago, and he is getting married in a year’s time.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Some first-timers were given queue numbers that far exceeded the number of flats available for booking, while others were not even given a queue number to begin with, especially when balance flats are put on sale.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I can understand why some young couples are only interested in an SBF.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: If they have put off starting a family for two years trying to secure a flat, they may not want to wait another three more years for a BTO flat with their biological clock ticking away.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: How can HDB help these young couples own their first matrimonial flats with less stress and more certainty as the future of our next generation depends on them?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Some of them were told to spread their options further if they want to secure a BTO or SBF flat, but that will mean living further away from their parents who, more often than not, would be the first port of call to help when they are starting their own families.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: And if their parents are living in a mature estate, who can fault these first-timer applicants for wanting to secure a new flat in and around the popular estate?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Next, would HDB consider offering balance flats to young couples who were unsuccessful in previous attempts to secure their first flats, be it in the same development or not, so as to help them secure a flat sooner?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The Lift Upgrading Programme (LUP) has benefited many households since the programme was launched in 2001.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: LUP has allowed many senior citizens to go out and meet their friends or watch the world go by at the playground or at the void deck, even if they are on mobility aids.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: In short, LUP has given these senior citizens a comforting and reassuring sense of independence at an age when they may have to be home alone.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: In my conversations with the affected residents living in these blocks of flats, I can sense their anxiety and despair about ageing in an environment with no direct lift access.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: To some of these residents, their flats are not built of concrete alone, but of memories.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: They would like to age in a place they call home.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: But without direct lift access, these residents may become prisoners in their own homes over time.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Some residents told me they need to make special arrangement just to bring their aged parents to visit the doctor.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Some elderly residents would prefer not to go out at all, and they would depend on their neighbours to help them with the errands.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: It is good to give these residents an indication of the time required to resolve the lift access issue.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: While some HDB flats are challenging to implement 100% lift access, some are relatively easy to resolve.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: For those HDB flats with complicated structures, can HDB look into solutions like vertical platform lifts, which are suitable for wheelchair use, and rather compact and inexpensive to implement for short level access?

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: In all fairness, residents living in the remaining 150 blocks should also get the benefits of direct lift access.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I seek confirmation from the Ministry that effort is continuing to bring 100% lift access to these affected blocks in the near future.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Some of these issues are long-standing but such relief offered by HIP should not be short-lived.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The bulk of the costs of HIP is funded by taxpayers.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: These contractors are expected to deliver quality works and fixtures that commensurate with their winning bids at the very least.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: While wear and tear can continue over time in an old flat which has undergone HIP, spalling concrete or leaks cannot possibly resurface at the same spot shortly after the one-year Defects Liability Period (DLP).

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: It does not make sense to the affected residents that HIP is meant to resolve such long-standing issues for about a year at the very most.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Although there are not many such cases reported, it certainly lends weight to the fact that the upgrading works were not carried out properly for some of these flats in the first place.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: Next, I would like HDB to consult residents living on the ground floor before installing the new clothes drying racks in their units.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: The new rack compromises the safety of residents living on the ground floor as the structure will allow intruders to gain easy access into their units via the kitchen windows using the new rack as a support.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: I hope these old flats can be rejuvenated with better connectivity to help the elderly access e-services easily with dedicated smart devices.

speaker: Mr Png Eng Huat
text: More importantly, I hope all physical barriers to active ageing would be removed completely by then, inside and outside the flats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: However, over time, substantial differences have developed among HDB estates.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, may I have your permission to display a slide on the screen?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Let us compare the third lowest and the third highest HDB town by resale price.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: As a percentage of the mean resale price that year, the range was from about 75% to 120% in 1990, and from about 80% to 150% in 2018.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Similar figures hold for other types of flats.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: However, rising incomes and wealth among better-off Singaporeans appear to be driving prices up because these HDB towns are close to the city centre and well-connected to amenities.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Let us also consider the policy of favouring private development over public use, for high-value locations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: When the bus interchange at Yishun, where I live, was redeveloped, the HDB commercial centre there was demolished.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: The land was integrated into the private Northpoint City development.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Hon Members will have seen similar examples in their own constituencies.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: When I wear my economist's hat, I see why the private sector should maximise the value of that land.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Otherwise, we would have to subsidise it heavily.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: But this is the heart of the problem.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: When value is assigned by the market, it is those with the ability to pay who will get to live closer to Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) stations, closer to the city centre, closer to any amenity that people want.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: I believe public housing should act as an integrator.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Public housing must play a role in checking the forces of segregation that would otherwise put rich Singaporeans in the most desirable places, and poor Singaporeans everywhere else.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: Can we consider alternative forms of HDB ownership in high-valuation areas to ensure that public housing continues to integrate Singaporeans of all types, and lower-income Singaporeans have a wide choice of locations to stay?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira
text: This may include equity-sharing with HDB or shorter-term leases with guaranteed subsidised resettlement on lease expiry.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, I am sure every Member in this House would have come across two groups of residents at our Meet-the-People Sessions relating to BTO and resale flats.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The first group would be young couples asking us to write to HDB because they have not been lucky in getting their BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Some even told me that they are delaying having a child because they wanted to have a place of their own first.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I have always tried to persuade such couples to consider buying a resale flat instead.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I will explain that resale prices have softened.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I also highlighted to these couples that a resale flat often has a larger floor size.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, although the absolute price may be higher, but the per square foot price may be lower.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Unfortunately, even after my "sales pitch", most couples still tell me that they still want BTO because the absolute price of resale flat is still much higher than BTO and they are also concerned about the high cost of renovation for a resale flat as well as the shorter lease period.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, the second group of residents are those who are unable to sell their current HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: They may have purchased another BTO or upgraded to private housing and when the time comes for them to sell, they were unable to do so due to the weak market conditions.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: So, we have a situation where there are too many buyers for BTO flats and too few buyers for resale flats.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Having young couples move into a mature estate through buying resale flats is also good so that the estate does not grow old.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Young families can bring vibrancy and diversity to older estates.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It also lessens the pressure on childcare and other school facilities in the newer estates where there are too many BTO flats.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Chairman, I have a few suggestions to make today.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For new BTO flats, I expect that the implied dollar value subsidy per unit is larger for a 5-room flat than for a 3-room flat.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: But conversely, the CPF Housing Grant for first-timers buying resale flat is smaller for a bigger unit.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The current system is an indirect form of means-testing which is not done for couples buying BTO.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In fact, there are many intangible benefits for young couples to stay near their parents.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: For children with both parents working, it is important that their grandparents are around to show them love and also pass down traditional values.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: In summary, I hope HDB can do more to make the purchase of resale flats more attractive to young couples.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It is a waste of resources to build ever more BTO flats to meet demand while there are many perfectly fine resale flats available for sale.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Louis Ng, you can take both your cuts together.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: When a child is involved, it could get even harder.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Going through a divorce is an emotionally draining period and our policies might make it more acrimonious, especially for the lower-income.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Couples know that if they get shared care and control of their child, they will have to fight each other for subsidised public housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If one party gets sole care and control, then he or she is guaranteed subsidised public housing.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Is it in the best interest of the child for their parents to have a more acrimonious divorce?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If shared care and control is a Court judgment, should not our housing policies make it possible to enforce the judgment to protect the best interests of the child?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Unlike those above 35, who qualify for public housing under the Singles Scheme, those under 35 can only qualify on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: With a median household income of only $600 in 2017, lacking the cash component of the Baby Bonus, and often lacking family support, single unwed parents really need our help.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am grateful that HDB has approved several housing appeals I have made for them.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But this case-by-case basis approach adds unnecessary stress to an already stressed parent.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: A safe and stable home is a fundamental need for every child, and our housing policy should be child-centric.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For a start, can the Minister consider providing rental housing to single unwed parents under 35 years old with a monthly household income below a certain amount and who lack family support?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can we accept their applications at the HDB counters like any other HDB flat application?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Let us not tell the applicant that they do not technically qualify, that it is subject to a case-by-case review, and that they should see their Member of Parliament to submit an appeal.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Chairman, I asked the Minister last year about retirement village models that could be transplanted here to give our seniors diverse options for retirement housing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: For public housing, Kampung Admiralty, with its active ageing hub and placement of amenities within walking distance, I would like to ask the Minister about the possibility of retrofitting our public housing estates to approximate the Kampung Admiralty model.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Future seniors who have different financial abilities need aspirations about active ageing.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the Lien Foundation and NTUC Income study, our future seniors prefer retirement villages to nursing homes by a large majority.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is a need to diversify elderly housing options.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These facilities allow seniors to enjoy their independence and maintain an active lifestyle while staff help with chores and monitor their health.

speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: What are the possibilities and limitations to introducing the development of affordable privately-run assisted living facilities here in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Failure to sell the flat is a genuine concern faced by some minority buyers, and for the elderly, this is of even greater concern when they need the money for their living expenses or illness, if they are not open to other options, such as renting and the lease buyback scheme.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: Already, the age of a flat in a mature estate could pose a challenge in selling the flat.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: And now, coupled with the limitations of the EIP, the difficulty of selling is doubled.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: I have seen a number of residents above 65 years old having difficulty selling their bigger flats and to monetise them because of the EIP.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: What are the challenges for the elderly in using these schemes?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: How will the Government help to better facilitate such schemes?

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: The main reason behind my suggestion is to pass on to our seniors the savings arising from lower capital expenditure involved in converting schools to homes.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Also, there are other advantages, as noted by the hon Minister in his written reply, such as the relatively large size of the school plot which can accommodate a good number of persons and the favourable location as, usually, schools tend to be located near neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Yesterday, we heard from the hon Minister for Education on his plans to redevelop junior colleges which will eventually result in more vacant schools.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I would be grateful for an update on this matter from the Minister.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: There are good examples of proper rest areas for outsourced workers provided in some buildings, such as JTC Summit, Inland Revenue Authority of Singapore, the seven new hawker centres and many others.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, there are buildings that may not have designated rest areas at the service buyers' premises, and these may not have been catered for when the premises were built.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In this aspect, I opine that the URA can play a critical role to make this happen if the Development Charge (DC) can be waived if the building owners set aside an area as rest areas.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: DC is a tax levied when planning permission is granted to carry out development projects that increase the value of land, such as rezoning to a higher value use or increased plot ratio.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: DC can run into thousands of dollars depending on the geographical area and usage.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This may encourage building owners to provide rest areas for the outsourced workers as well.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Many big projects continue to be awarded to foreign contractors.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Many local contractors hope that our Government can walk the talk and support our local contractors.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: This can help them build up track records and also stay afloat during this difficult period.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I appreciate the Government’s effort to ensure a more sustainable environment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: But it is unfortunate that there is no grace period.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Additionally, contractors, architects and engineers face a lot of red tape in the process of their work.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: They told me that road openings, service diversions and Land Transport Authority (LTA) clearances cause them the most headaches.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: As an example, one developer paid a few hundred thousand dollars for service diversion.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Subsequently, no existing services were found on site.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The developer, after several years and many rounds of appeal, has yet to get back his money.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Also, planning approvals often take a long time.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: After dealing with one written direction, very often, agencies come back with another new set of written directions, and then it is back to the drawing board, and seeking approvals again.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: In a tender, if there are 10 tenderers, 10 contractors will build their own 3D modelling from scratch.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Can the project architect not issue 3D model to all tenderers instead?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: How does the Ministry arrive at the man-year entitlement allocation?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Many contractors said the current allocation is insufficient for a project.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Because of increasing safety demands, every potentially dangerous job requires a watchman while the foreign worker quota is being tightened.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I hope the Government will re-examine all the above together with MOM.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Mr Chairman, park connectors are used by people for strolls, walking their babies or pet dogs, or for exercises, such as briskwalking, jogging or cycling.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: They are also used by people to get to nearby MRT stations or bus stops.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Depending on the locations of these park connectors, they can be really busy at certain times of the day or week.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Bicycles, e-scooters, mobility scooters, wheelchairs, skatescooters and strollers compete for use with people and pets on foot.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As a regular user, I have always been concerned about the safety of park connectors.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I am particularly concerned about the uncertainty regarding the appropriate use of the lanes provided on park connectors.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Mr Chairman, with your permission, may I show a photograph so that people can have an idea of the lane marking I am going to refer to?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Is the lane marked with the figure of a person walking only reserved for people on foot?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Who is allowed to use the part marked "PCN" or park connector network?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: If so, is it not dangerous for other users, such as cyclists and personal mobility device (PMD) users, to use it while people are walking on it from both directions?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: In practice, many people walk on both lanes, and cyclists and PMD users are often left weaving through the traffic on both lanes frequently unsafely, especially during peak periods.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The lane marked with the figure of a person walking is narrower than the part marked PCN.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: It is too narrow for concurrent two-directional use when, say, someone is pushing a stroller or walking a big dog.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I first raised this issue last September during the Second Reading of the Land Transport Enforcement Measures Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I filed a Parliamentary Question with MND last month asking what actions have been taken to promote the safe use of park connectors by different users, including safe and orderly adherence to the respective lane markings for users on foot and for PCN users.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: The Minister did not address the issue of adherence to lane markings.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: So, I would like to ask the Minister today: how are park users supposed to use the park connectors safely according to the lane markings?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Will the authority educate the public on the safe usage of park connectors?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I use the park connectors almost every day, and I have never seen any signage or advisory on this issue.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I have never seen any enforcement being carried out, whether it is illegal usage, for example, speeding by cyclists or PMD users, or cyclists or PMD users using the part marked of the figure of a person walking.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I have, however, seen quite a few accidents and many near misses, and a recent accident involving a young child and an e-scooter on a park connector prompted me to raise this again.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Louis Ng, please take your three cuts.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Cat abandonment is one of the reasons for an increase in the stray cat population.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It also causes problems as cat feeders struggle with the sudden increase in numbers and residents also suffer disamenities.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: It is easy to enforce these laws with dogs as dogs are microchipped and licensed and we can trace the owner.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: She left the pet carrier there with her details.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: But how many owners will abandon their cat and leave traces of their details?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: In other cases, it is not so straightforward.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister provide an update on the progress of the programme?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Has there been strong public support and what kinds of concerns have been raised and how have we addressed them?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister also share whether we will be adopting a similar approach for wild animals where we focus on science-based approaches that tackle the root of the problem and address both residents' concerns and animal welfare concerns?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Recently, there has been much concern about the environmental impact of the Cross Island Line and the Mandai developments.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: There will be similar developments in the future, and many have argued for mandating Environmental Impact Assessments (EIAs).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Earlier this month, I asked the Minister if EIAs will be made mandatory for construction works near national parks or nature reserves.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can we also mandate that EIA consultants file their final reports to the authorities rather than the developers so as to ensure their independence?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: For construction works in or near sensitive security areas, can the Ministry make EIAs public after removing sensitive data related to national security?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: The goal, to improve service delivery and coordinate across agencies, is the right one, and certainly welcomed by my residents.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: What are some specific and tangible benefits that residents have experienced, and what can they look forward to in the coming years?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: Equally important, how are MSO and the municipal agencies harnessing technology to respond more effectively and efficiently to residents’ issues?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: We have all become spoilt by online service providers that cater to our whims with a few swipes of our smartphones.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: While we do not expect instant responses or solutions to every problem, service gaps will seem more painful for residents.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: What plans does MSO have to use technology both in the front end, for example, using apps, and backend, for example, using AI and automation of basic services to improve service delivery?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Why is this important as we continue to encourage adoption of the app for more widespread usage?

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: It is not because we do it for the sake of becoming a digital nation, but truly to reap the benefits of big data, efficiency in response and to bring it further by involving community and agency resources in the vicinity.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: In that respect, I have a few areas to highlight for consideration.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: First, focus resources on the critical or frequently raised topics.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: For example, today, the lift is a common facility that is widely used in HDB.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: While it falls under the purview of the Town Council, the usual feedback route is through the Town Council service hotline.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: If there is a case of a man trapped in the lift, it will take longer for support to arrive on site as it needs multiple calls at the backend.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: This, compared to if the app is already connected to the lift service provider or the rescue unit to seek help in case there are emergencies or medical conditions for the person trapped, the latter would have been more efficient.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Second, expand the app's capability beyond a feedback tool.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Besides providing feedback on municipal issues observed on the ground, consideration should be made for the tool to also serve as a channel for ideas from the ground on how we can improve situations or designs.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: I have heard thoughtful feedback from residents on municipal matters due to their work expertise or experience in similar situations.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: While we understand not all ideas are feasible due to different constraints, but it can become a useful platform for the community and the agencies to share and evolve ideas which are practical for the local context.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Third, connectivity of app to community resources for the elderly.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Today, a caregiver or the family member probably has to download many apps or search online for information on suitable services for their seniors in the community.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: The idea I am raising is to provide more convenience for the caregivers and for them to understand or be notified if there are upcoming municipal works or unintended disruptions which may cause difficulties for the seniors who are less mobile.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: As a first step, I would encourage MSO to think of how we can put community resource information on the app based on regions.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: One, to enable the community to know what services are available in the vicinity that are suitable for seniors.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Should this be successful and have more capability in future, we can connect our seniors to be a part of the app.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: Many would say it is difficult to get the elderly to be digitally inclined.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: This could be true for the Pioneers today, but this will not be the case for the Merdekas and the younger cohorts in future.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling
text: It is useful for us to think on a longer horizon and more effectively utilise the technology space.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: Technology, when applied correctly, can enable Government agencies to deliver smarter and more efficient services to meet increasing demand and rising expectations.

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: How are MSO and the municipal agencies harnessing technology to respond more efficiently and effectively to residents' issues?

speaker: Mr Amrin Amin (Sembawang)
text: Good municipal service delivery is about understanding the needs of the local community and ensuring that they are met.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Mr Chairman, like fellow Members of the House, I get my fair share of feedback on municipal issues from residents, whether face-to-face or through emails and social media.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Common ones include littering, bird and cat feeding, not cleaning up after their pet dogs, noise nuisance and so on.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: I do appreciate these feedback because they help us understand the ground better and relevant agencies can target their attention and actions towards more specific areas.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: After all, residents are naturally more familiar with their own environment as they use the area on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: They are the best eyes, ears and closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: In other words, an area is full of litter because of two possible reasons: the cleaner has not done his work properly, or the public are not disposing of their litter properly.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: For most common areas in the estate, sweeping is done once in the morning.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: Therefore, if someone throws a piece of litter after the cleaner has swept the floor, it will be there till the next morning.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: When I receive feedback on littering, I am interested to know whether is it not clean, not cleaned or not cleaned yet.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: With the information, we can then decide on the necessary intervention.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: For example, in the case of littering, it could mean a closer monitoring of the work of the cleaner, or public education on responsible disposal of littering, or, perhaps, the National Environment Agency (NEA) should be putting up CCTV cameras to catch errant litterbugs in areas where littering is very prevalent.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: I am glad that MSO, with its OneService app, has made the process much easier, effective and hassle-free.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: However, there are municipal issues which clearly warrant enforcement leading to prosecution, for example, illegal parking, whether is it at season parking lots, handicap-accessible lots, loading and unloading bays, along double yellow lines or at the void deck.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng (Tampines)
text: There are also cases of motorcycles riding on pavements, sheltered linkways and void decks.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank Members Mr Baey Yam Keng, Mr Ong Teng Koon, Mr Amrin Amin and Miss Cheryl Chan for their questions on the MSO, and also earlier, Ms Denise Phua, for her positive mention of MSO in her speech on MSF.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: MSO was set up with the belief that public services should be focused on our residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Residents can now expect more timely responses to their feedback.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For cases that require multiple agencies to work together, we have improved case routing processes and integrated agencies' feedback systems for greater efficiency in case management.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Last year, we introduced the Local Infrastructure Projects scheme to enable MSO and agencies to assess residents' requests for small-scale infrastructure in a timely manner.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, we jointly evaluated a request supported by the Citizens' Consultative Committee for a footpath with lighting under the Sengkang West vehicular bridge.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For the safety of residents, the Public Utilities Board tapped on the scheme as the implementing agency to build the infrastructure.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Their efficiency in meeting the needs of the residents won them compliments from the residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As Mr Ong Teng Koon, Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Amrin Amin have suggested, technology offers us great potential in achieving better services with high operational productivity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: As part of the Smart Nation movement, we have been harnessing technology to deliver smarter municipal services.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have started enabling residents to do more with the OneService app to meet their diverse needs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This year, we will progressively introduce new features to transform the app into a one-stop community platform not just to report feedback, but also to perform transactions, engage one another and access information.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, residents will soon be able to book and pay for neighbourhood facilities, such as the barbeque pits near their block through the app.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Motorists will be able to obtain paperless Electronic Parking Systems receipts for HDB and URA car parks through the app, which can be useful for tracking expenditure or claims.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Residents can also receive alerts on happenings in their neighbourhood, such as roadworks and hawker centre closures for maintenance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will be implementing these enhancements in the coming year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: And I thank Miss Cheryl Chan for her suggestions on how we can deepen connections and community involvement through the app.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We will continue to engage our users and partners with these ideas as we transform the OneService app.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Next, we are working with our partners to respond better to residents, by using technology to re-engineer our processes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: First, we have implemented case routing using artificial intelligence (AI).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This enables cases to be routed automatically to the right agency, freeing up officers to focus their efforts on solving more complex problems.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Second, agencies can access one another's proposed and ongoing projects through a new Infrastructure Works Dashboard.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They can use system tools in the Dashboard to deconflict overlapping works for better coordination.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Hence, we can minimise inconveniences arising from infrastructure works to residents.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
