text: In the future, we want to bring about more service improvements through the Municipal Services Productivity Fund introduced in 2017.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: An example of a funded project is Parking.sg, developed by Government Technology Agency, HDB and URA.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Besides making it more convenient to pay for parking, removing the need for the paper coupon system, Parking.sg has actually resulted in savings for motorists.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Nearly half of parking sessions are ended early, and drivers have been able to get more than $3.3 million in total refunded to them for unused time so far.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: So, we have extended the fund and set aside $25 million for agencies to tap on over the next five years.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We have approved two new projects under the extended fund for drones by the Singapore Land Authority for early detection of maintenance issues, and a trial deployment of compactor litter bins by NEA for more efficient waste collection.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: In total, we have awarded $5.2 million for six projects, and expect about five times that in productivity gains.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng and Miss Cheryl Chan asked about the efforts of MSO and our municipal agencies in partnering the community in tackling issues and building greater ownership.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: They highlighted the value of residents' feedback, which MSO can study using data analytics to understand root causes and develop more effective and targeted solutions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We fully agree with them and are progressively doing so as we build up our database to tackle complex issues.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Mr Baey Yam Keng asked if we could enable residents to easily alert agencies through the OneService app for municipal offences that may require enforcement action, such as illegal parking.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: We are studying this carefully with the agencies, taking into account the need to ensure responsible reporting for the purpose of enforcement.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Beyond giving feedback, when private individuals and groups come forward, we can tap on diverse ideas, deeper knowledge and stronger networks to solve our problems effectively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: This is why agencies are collaborating extensively with grassroots organisations, Community Development Councils, Institutes of Higher Learning (IHLs) and the public.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: These partnerships enable us to harness ideas, co-create and pilot solutions for issues with the local community.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: A group of National University of Singapore (NUS) students participated in the Youth Challenge and designed rubbish bins that allowed people to have some fun in expressing their opinions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, people could indicate their preference for roasted versus steamed chicken rice by throwing their litter into the corresponding bin.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The students tested their idea and found that people are more minded to discard their trash in the bins.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: The students gained from understanding gamification and its impact on behavioural change.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Checking if the gravitraps set up by NEA to monitor the mosquito population, whether they are in good condition, is an example.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: Going forward, we will enable residents to put up simple activities on the app.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: For example, residents can help spot missing pet dogs or share household tools with one another.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: But we also want to do this with residents because municipal issues ultimately impact us all in our daily lives.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Grace Fu Hai Yien)
text: By so doing, we can build a better home for all, together.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chairman, may I show some visuals at the appropriate junctures to illustrate some points I am going to make?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, our infrastructure resilience; second, climate resilience; and third, social resilience.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We often take infrastructure resilience to mean how strong and durable our existing structures are, and how well we maintain them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This certainly is important as our buildings start to age.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But resilience is also about designing and building better to meet tomorrow's challenges, so that our buildings can accommodate higher-density living, changing lifestyle needs and also withstand tougher weather conditions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This means adopting innovative solutions in design and construction.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That is why MND continues to invest heavily in research and development in the urban and infrastructure sector.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In recent years, it partnered the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) to develop the Integrated Environmental Modeller (IEM).

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: IEM is a 3D modelling software that predicts how environmental conditions interact with our town plans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The software can, for example, try to simulate how wind flows through different urban features and open spaces, and where solar heat is more likely to build up.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This helps our town planners take some of the guesswork out of designing a more liveable and sustainable estate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They can plan better for open spaces to enjoy good ventilation, and plant trees and greenery in the right places to help bring down ambient temperatures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Singapore can be a thought leader in producing innovative urban solutions like IEM.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We are both compact and well-connected, which is an ideal living testbed for new ideas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Innovations developed here have the potential to be useful in other dense, tropical cities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They are currently in talks with the industry to see how IEM can be adapted for commercial use.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: I hear that they are even looking to bring it overseas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will continue to support promising research under the Cities of Tomorrow programme, which builds on the success of the Land and Liveability National Innovation Challenge.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But all of them aim to develop practical solutions to the multifaceted challenges that exist in our built environment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, in construction technology, we are investing in innovations, such as 3D printing, to build faster, safer and more cost-effectively.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In facilities management, we are studying how robots and data analytics can make the job of inspecting building facades safer and more efficiently.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Ultimately, these innovations aim to improve the lives of people and ensure that our city meets the demands not just of today but of tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Various Members have spoken about the importance of being responsive to the threats and effects of climate change.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is especially critical for small, low-lying states like us to act decisively to protect ourselves.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have conducted studies to examine the risks and impacts of sea level rise and invested in clean-tech solutions, so as to move towards becoming a more low-carbon society.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Minister Lawrence Wong will speak more about this tomorrow.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Today, I will speak about an important response to climate change – protecting the diversity and resilience of our natural and urban ecosystems.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a comprehensive effort that requires planning at different levels.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, at the design level, our colleagues at the National Parks Board (NParks) have put in a lot of thought to embed climate resilience features into our urban green spaces.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At one-north Park, specially chosen wildflowers and grasses help to filter storm water runoff naturally.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These plants then also serve as a habitat for various species of butterflies, birds and aquatic wildlife, bringing them into the city.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our Nature Ways, such as the one shown here in Tampines, replicate the tiered structure of a tropical forest with native trees and shrubs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, these are not just streetscape but are grown in a particular way to replicate some natural structures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They provide important ecosystem services to people and facilitate ecological connectivity for some species.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Over the next 10 years, we will do more to regenerate forests in our Nature Parks as well as Nature Reserves.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Third, underpinning all this work are our continued efforts to conserve our native flora and fauna.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: What Members see in the video is the Neptune’s Cup Sponge, which is one of the species being carefully rehabilitated in Singapore waters.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It was thought to be globally extinct since 1908.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But it was rediscovered in Singapore in 2011, the first known rediscovery of this species in the world.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, you see this work of NParks officers relocating it to afford it better protection from the elements.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Another species in our recovery programme is the Harlequin Butterfly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It is rare and little is known about its biology.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But NParks has been studying it closely in the field and has been relocating it to new sites to establish more populations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members also pointed out that development should not come at the expense of greenery.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We would like to assure Mr Louis Ng, Mr Chong Kee Hiong, Mr Ong Teng Koon and Mr Pritam Singh that maintaining and enhancing our greenery will continue to be a key pillar of our urban planning strategy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In our post-Independence years, this was what set us apart from other cities with similar growth strategies.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Indeed, as Minister Heng Swee Keat said in his Budget round-up speech, greening is part of our identity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But our small size as a city-state means that our land and resources are scarce and finite, and the tensions and tradeoffs for us when it comes to land use are magnified many times, compared to larger countries.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is a reality we live with every day, and our planners are always seized with these challenges.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we have to continue to be judicious about how we use land to meet our needs as a city and as a country, while ensuring that we safeguard land for the aspirations of our children and our future generations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In this regard, any decision to clear land and forest cover is not taken lightly.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If we do, it is a decision we make after very careful deliberation and inter-agency discussion, taking into account Singaporeans’ needs and the many tradeoffs involved.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are not just difficult tradeoffs in the present day between greenery and biodiversity on the one hand, and housing and jobs on the other, but tradeoffs between the present and the future, between land use for today's needs and keeping land for our children and grandchildren and generations not yet born.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, in response to Mr Louis Ng's question, we work to ensure that when development does take place, proposals are thoroughly examined for any potential environmental impacts, among other issues.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Those who propose development close to these areas are required to consult our technical agencies on their plans together with URA and MND.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We take a prudent approach to this consultation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If we have reason to believe that a project may significantly impact the environment, then the developer will be asked by technical agencies to conduct a further environmental study.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We would like to assure the Member that studies are undertaken in an independent and objective manner by specialists who have every interest to maintain their professional standing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The study reports are also carefully assessed by the technical agencies, such as NParks, the Agri-Food and Veterinary Authority, Maritime Port Authority and NEA, to ensure their adequacy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: That said, our review of the EIA framework is ongoing.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: MND and the technical agencies are studying how best to strengthen our policies and processes to ensure the framework remains robust for the future.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This brings me to my third and final area of focus.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our green spaces not only contribute to our climate resilience, they also bring people together and are an important part of our social resilience.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Singaporeans have reason to be proud of our distinctive greenery and rich biodiversity.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our common spaces allow us to interact with one another and bond with our family and friends.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For example, our community gardeners tend to more than 1,400 Community-in-Bloom gardens across the island.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Our Biodiversity Beach Patrol volunteers help monitor key stretches of our beaches.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Meanwhile, NParks' extensive Friends of the Park communities continue to see people from all walks of life and all interests coming together with a common love for nature and open spaces.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Dennis Tan highlighted concerns about the safe use of our park connectors and showed us a photograph of that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks has installed more safety features to enhance the safe use of PCNs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Additional lighting, speed regulating strips and advisory signs have been put up.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: NParks has also installed advisory signs at high usage parks and park connectors to remind users to stay on track and give way.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And NParks conducts outreach programmes to promote the safe use of park connectors, including lane usage and appropriate speed limits.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And NParks is working together with LTA on joint enforcement efforts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But the Friends of the PCN have also been contributing to our efforts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Chaired by avid cyclist and nature lover Mr Woon Tai Woon, the Friends of PCN have led the charge on ground-up initiatives, reaching out to PCN users to promote safe riding, like helping with track painting and public signage, encouraging safe riding etiquette through the "Share the Track" programme and, most recently, creating a video promoting the responsible use of PMDs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will also activate more community nodes for citizens to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In 2017, we announced the start of trail enhancement works along the Rail Corridor.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The continuous green trail stretches 24 km from the north to the south of Singapore and is used by many as a place to cycle and trek.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We continue to ensure that our residential communities are served well by high-quality social and community facilities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This means ensuring that community facilities are right-sited and sized appropriately to support cohesive and multi-generational neighbourhoods.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It will also have a cycling path that connects to the larger Punggol cycling network around it.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The mix of amenities was carefully planned so as to meet the needs of the current demographic of residents and, as Punggol evolves, so, too, will the offerings at Punggol Town Hub.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah made a request to increase heavy vehicle parking options in Yishun.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Public heavy vehicle parking is popular as it tends to be cheaper and closer to residential areas, and that is where the tension arises.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These residents were concerned about heavy vehicles entering residential built-up areas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But of course, it is usually more convenient for drivers to park near homes, especially given the hours that they operate.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Unfortunately, while we plan carefully to ensure sufficient heavy vehicle lots at a national level, it is not always possible to fully meet local demand, especially near heavily built-up residential areas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These are in relation to site constraints, concerns of safety, noise and other disamenities.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We encourage drivers to look into private heavy vehicle lot options as well as alternatives in neighbouring areas.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we also encourage employers to take responsibility and help their drivers find the right spaces to park their company vehicles.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we will certainly work with Er Dr Lee Bee Wah to look at the requirements in Nee Soon.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some car parks already allow day and night season parking.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Since private cars, heavy vehicles and commercial vehicles tend to need parking at different times, available space is often already used optimally.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Separately, agencies have also allowed parking lots that do not have traffic and site constraints to double up as heavy vehicle spaces for short time periods.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But we continue to look out for other car parks which can be further optimised to support dual use and will continue to explore the ideas that the Members have raised.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have come far together, but we have more to do to build a thriving and dynamic city, develop comfortable homes and neighbourhoods, and protect our natural and built environment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We look forward to the continued support of all our Members.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, at the appropriate junctures, may I show some slides?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Mr Alex Yam asked about our plans to create a future-ready built environment (BE) sector that supports the nation's changing needs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Since then, we have been partnering the industry, unions and IHLs to implement the ITMs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To drive change at the workforce, firm and ecosystem level, the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) set up the BuildSG transformation office last year to partner the industry in growing progressive firms and preparing the workforce for the future.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BuildSG has been working with the Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) to help them build expertise in the three transformation areas of Design for Manufacturing and Assembly (DfMA), Integrated Digital Delivery (IDD) and Green Buildings.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: These plans underline the TACs' commitment to guide firms and individuals through the transformation journey.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA is also partnering industry stakeholders through the IDD Steering Committee to guide the development of IDD and encourage greater integration across the construction value chain.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Dr Teo Ho Pin noted, Building Information Modelling (BIM) is not yet seamlessly adopted across different project parties.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The intent is to facilitate the use of a single BIM model across the construction value chain, from design to construction, and to operations and maintenance.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have also undertaken various initiatives to upgrade and augment the BE workforce, who are key to industry transformation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Beyond infrastructure, manpower capability is also something that we need to build.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: First, IHLs will be updating their curricula to better equip undergraduates with skills and competencies to support transformation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As a start, NUS will pilot an interdisciplinary module on prefabricated prefinished volumetric construction (PPVC) later this year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The pilot module will not only familiarise students with this technology but also expose them to real work conditions where different stakeholders work together to deliver a project.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Second, the Committee has developed internship guidelines to help companies structure more effective internships.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Good internships offer students a valuable opportunity to get a taste of work in the BE sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The hands-on experience also better prepare students for joining the workforce.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, Ms Tan Zi Rui went on a year-long internship with Aurecon while studying at the Singapore Institute of Technology.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: She helped to retrofit buildings with energy-efficient cooling systems and gained engineering experience.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Aurecon was also able to assess Zi Rui's technical and behavioural competencies and offered her the iBuildSG undergraduate scholarship, and subsequently a full-time position.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is wonderful to see young women joining the BE sector and, in this case, the construction industry as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Committee's guidelines aim to help more firms and students benefit from such positive internship experiences.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I encourage firms to refer to them on BCA's Building Careers portal when planning your internship programmes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Third, the Committee will upgrade and augment the industry's competencies through enhancing continuing education and training.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Committee is developing (a) a skills framework to identify skills and competencies of the future and guide training programmes to help professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) remain relevant, as well as (b) a leadership framework to groom a core group of industry leaders.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will also continue to support firms in training and bringing in mid-career professionals through Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Last year, we introduced the PCP for BIM Professionals.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: After learning about the promising career prospects of a BIM modeller, Mr Mohamad Saifullizan Bin Abd Rahman took up the PCP.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: He has been receiving structured training in essential BIM skills, as well as on-the-job training with his industry sponsor, Lum Chang Building Contractors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To help more people like Saiful enter the BE sector, BCA is now working with Workforce Singapore to expand the PCP offerings to other BE transformation areas, such as for professionals supporting DfMA projects and offsite facilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will also do more to improve the attractiveness of construction industry jobs.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The use of productive technologies already improves working conditions and can create attractive new jobs, such as prefabrication supervisors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As Mr Zainal Sapari pointed out, it is also important to provide rest areas for workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I announced at MOM's COS session yesterday that we will be looking into companies' practices in this regard.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MND will also look at how best to ensure adequate provision of rest areas from a planning perspective.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Another important aspect of good jobs is remuneration.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: With the move towards higher skilled jobs, wages should also keep up.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I urge industry leaders to continue your efforts in enhancing pay and career prospects for employees, so as to build up a strong local core of PMETs to support sustainable industry transformation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Government will also do our part to ensure that wages remain competitive.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA is working with the industry to phase in implementation, while ensuring sufficient lead time for buyers and firms to adjust.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I am heartened to see progressive firms adopt productive construction technologies like DfMA.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Take, for instance, INSTAD Pre Fabrication Pte Ltd, which set up a facility for prefabricated mechanical, electrical and plumbing (MEP) systems in 2017.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Through automation, the firm has achieved higher construction quality, with up to 40% time savings and 60% productivity improvements.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Workers in the MEP factory also enjoy improved working conditions similar to the manufacturing sector, compared to traditional construction sites.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We want to support more firms in their transformation journey and shift the industry towards adopting productive technologies like DfMA.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To do this, we will need to complement existing funding schemes and manpower development initiatives with changes to our foreign manpower policies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Currently, construction projects are subject to the Man-Year-Entitlement (MYE) framework, which manages foreign worker numbers at the project level.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: MYE quotas are allocated to main contractors based on project type and value.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Main contractors then decide how to allocate these quotas to their subcontractors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have received feedback from the industry that such an arrangement is not optimal, as Er Dr Lee Bee Wah had also fed back in her speech.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For example, a main contractor may only pass on a small proportion of the allocated MYE quota to subcontractors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: DfMA facilities are also not allocated MYE quotas directly as they are not project-based.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, most workers in DfMA facilities are employed on the higher MYE waiver levy rates.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This means that the manpower cost for offsite DfMA works is typically higher, compared to onsite works at construction sites.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: While we have received industry feedback, as Er Dr Lee Bee Wah said about the allocation of MYE quotas, increasing our reliance on foreign workers cannot be the way forward.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Instead, to better align our manpower policies with our transformation outcomes, we will have to review the existing MYE framework for the construction sector.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We want to replace the MYE with a system that better enables the industry to optimise their foreign workforce, be it onsite or at DfMA facilities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will take time and BCA will consult the industry in working out these changes to the MYE framework.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Firms on the OCSS will be able to hire an allocated number of workers at MYE levy rates.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This will lower the cost premium for DfMA and hopefully encourage more firms to shift towards offsite work.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA will be engaging eligible companies to explain the details of the scheme, which will be implemented later this year.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah and Mr Ang Wei Neng underscored the importance of efficient and streamlined regulations and processes for construction projects.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The Inter-Agency Coordinating Committee (IACC) was established by BCA in 2011 to resolve cross-agency regulatory issues.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Instead of meeting only when issues are surfaced, the IACC has started to hold monthly meetings this year to proactively engage the industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Where there are changes to regulations, we will do what we can to help firms transition.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Specific to Er Dr Lee Bee Wah's feedback on the service diversion and others, we will take those on board and I will have a word with BCA to see how best we can help her.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked about rebates to help absorb the diesel duty increase.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As announced by the Minister for Finance, three years of road tax rebates will be provided for commercial diesel vehicles.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: The rebates will also apply to commercial vehicles used in the construction industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also provided specific feedback on services diversion works and the Workplace Safety and Health (WSH) regulations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As many of our projects are on brownfield sites, preparatory works, such as services diversion, may be required prior to development works.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: It is inefficient for the Government to undertake all such land preparations before tendering out sites for sale.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Instead, our approach is to make known in the tender documents any encumbrances onsite so that interested bidders can factor these accordingly into their timelines and tender price.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As for workplace safety, our WSH regulations adopt a risk-based approach for the supervision of high-risk construction works.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Supervisors need not be present at all times if the risks are sufficiently addressed, for example, by adequately briefing workers on the potential risks and the proper use of tools and safety equipment.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As I have elaborated in my MOM speech yesterday, one of the strongest links to many of these fatalities is inexperienced workers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah also asked about our efforts to support local contractors.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We know that the industry has been experiencing a slowdown in recent years.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have introduced a number of measures to help.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To help local companies build up a track record, we have parceled out large infrastructure projects into smaller contracts that SMEs can take on and allowed smaller consultancy firms to band together to bid for higher value projects.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, to assure Er Dr Lee Bee Wah, we want to provide as much support as we can for local firms and, certainly, within our procurement guidelines.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: That is why we also have to continue to review our processes, policies and how we work with inter-agency regulations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is one of the reasons why we are looking at the MYE framework as well.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our longer-term focus remains on helping firms build capabilities and strengthen their competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We currently provide funding support to firms in various areas, including construction productivity, manpower development and research and innovation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This includes top-ups to two existing schemes, namely, the Productivity Innovation Project (PIP) and the Public Sector Construction Productivity Fund (PSCPF).

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: More than 300 firms have benefited from PIP, which co-funds capability development initiatives that improve site productivity.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: PSCPF supports Government agencies in procuring innovative and productive solutions for public sector projects.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Next, let me provide an update on the progress of the transformation efforts in the Real Estate industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: In April last year, BCA formed the tripartite Facilities Management Implementation Committee (FMIC) to transform the FM industry into one that is more productive and that leverages data analytics, predictive maintenance and smart solutions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To this end, FMIC, which comprises representatives from both the Government and the industry, has proposed recommendations in four areas, namely, (a) designing for maintainability; (b) enhancing maintenance productivity and quality through smart FM; (c) enhancing guidelines for FM procurement; and (d) ensuring adequate training and development of the FM workforce.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: While implementation details are being worked out, the public sector will take the lead to uplift the FM industry through various initiatives, such as by adopting outcome-based procurement guidelines.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This provides flexibility for FM service providers to focus on improving outcomes, instead of meeting headcount requirements.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the property transaction front, we will continue to enhance and streamline the transaction processes for users through automation and digitalisation.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: A key thrust is to make it easier for industry players to access property-related Government data, thereby enabling the automation of time-consuming administrative processes.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have done this for data related to rental transactions since February.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This means that checks, like whether a seller is the legal owner of the property, and whether a landlord is eligible to lease out an HDB unit, can now be done with the click of a button.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I believe this will benefit many, as rental transactions account for about 60% of all residential property transactions.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We encourage the industry to take advantage of this to streamline processes and better serve their customers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our long-term goal is to facilitate seamless and digitalised property transactions from start-to-finish.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To chart the way forward, the Council for Estate Agencies is chairing a digitalisation workgroup with representatives from both the Government and industry.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: By reducing the hardcopy documents and physical payments, consumers can spend less time on paperwork and queuing up at banks, and property agents, bankers and lawyers can focus on higher value-added services to customers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: As Mr Chong Kee Hiong noted in his speech, good infrastructure is essential in supporting our future economy.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We have a rigorous framework to ensure that our buildings are safe.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Developments involving structural works undergo checks to ensure that they have been designed and built according to the approved plans and building regulations.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Developers are required to engage trained professionals known as Qualified Persons and Accredited Checkers at various stages of the project, from the building design phase to supervising the construction works onsite, to certifying the works upon project completion.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: BCA also conducts sampling checks on building plans and targeted inspections on structural works and will take enforcement action against any party that contravenes the regulations.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to begin by thanking all Members who have spoken in support of the vulnerable, the less advantaged and the lower-income.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They are our fellow citizens, and Singapore is a shared home where we all belong.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Several Members have asked how we can better help tenants to have homes of their own.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: I would first like to share that the number of public rental households who moved into home ownership flats has increased steadily.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We are committed to helping more tenants move into home ownership.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Members have asked whether we are reviewing Fresh Start.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: This will allow more families to benefit from the scheme.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The new age limit will also apply for other schemes for parents with dependent children, namely, the Parenthood Priority Scheme, and the Assistance Scheme for Second-Timers who are divorced or widowed parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We have found through our experience that closer and more regular contact with families allows for early intervention to address issues that may emerge.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Support Programme will also take a holistic approach to strengthen them in various areas, such as financial management, family functioning and overall stability.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: The Support Programme will be overseen by the Ministry of Social and Family Development and they will appoint a service provider with social work expertise, and this will commence later this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Third, there are also families who applied for Fresh Start but who did not meet some of the criteria.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: If they are serious about Fresh Start and have good potential to meet the criteria fully, they can get special consideration to join.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: Once they join, they may book a Build-To-Order (BTO) 2-room flexi flat within one year like other Fresh Start families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: They will also get more intensive support under the Support Programme, focusing on the criteria that they did not meet.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
text: We look forward to partnering our tenants closely towards home ownership.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They have lived in a rental flat since 2006 with Mdm Narziah's daughter who is not pictured here.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Housing and Development Board (HDB) met Mdm Narziah last year to share about Fresh Start, and she decided to apply.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: She welcomed the assistance under the scheme and was appreciative that HDB officers met her in person to ask about her home ownership aspirations, and guided her through each step of buying a flat.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: She is now looking forward to her new flat in Tampines.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In my earlier speech a few days ago, I shared that HDB will introduce a dedicated team to provide personalised guidance for families towards home ownership.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The Home ownership Support Team will reach out to tenants who are more able to consider home ownership, for instance, those who possess a stable income and family stability.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Tenants who need advice on home ownership can also approach the team for help.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Miss Cheryl Chan and Mr Seah Kian Peng asked how we ensure that rents do not discourage tenants from working towards higher incomes and home ownership.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Our public rental rates are structured progressively to keep the subsidy allocation fair.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Nonetheless, to mitigate cliff effects, HDB waives the rent increase for up to two terms when tenants first cross the $800 income threshold, if their income remains less than $1,500.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In the last three years, about 5,200 households have benefited from this waiver.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB also reduces the rent for households on a case-by-case basis if they cannot afford it.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I would also like to emphasise that HDB does not ask tenants to leave solely because their income has increased past the ceiling of $1,500.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Instead, HDB will work with them on their home ownership options once they are ready.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To further encourage these households, we will not increase the rent for those who have made the downpayment for a new flat.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We hope this will put households in good stead for their next milestone as homeowners.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan suggested allowing tenants to buy over their rental flats.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We currently have no such plans, as there are many measures to help tenants buy a new flat from HDB.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This also maintains our rental flat supply for others who have no other housing options.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan also suggested improving the living environment in older rental blocks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB has consistently upgraded rental flats just as they do for sold flats.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But we want to do more, especially for older rental blocks built in the 1960s and 1970s.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As the Member highlighted, some blocks have long corridors with rental units on both sides.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As a result, the natural ventilation and light are more limited than those of newer designs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To address this, HDB will undertake works to create more openings along the corridors, by removing some flats on each floor of such blocks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will provide a permanent improvement for the residents in terms of the airflow and brightness of the block.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB has piloted this and the feedback from residents has been positive.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This shows a typical corridor of a block with units on both sides.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And this is a corridor at Block 217 Ang Mo Kio Avenue 1, where HDB piloted the upgrading works.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The works made a marked difference to the inside of each block – more common space, more sunlight, more ventilation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I have visited the older blocks and an improved block myself, and I think Members will agree with me that our proposed works will be a marked improvement.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will extend these works to more rental blocks and will provide more details in due course.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As some tenants may need to move for the improvement works, HDB will help them to move within the same or nearby blocks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB will work closely with local organisations and the relevant agencies to ensure a smooth transition.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But we want to do more, especially for older rental flats built in the 1960s and 1970s.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As Mr Lim Biow Chuan highlighted, some blocks have long corridors with rental units on both sides.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As a result, the natural ventilation and brightness are more limited than those of newer designs.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will provide a permanent improvement for the residents in terms of the airflow and brightness of the block.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB has piloted this and the feedback from residents has been positive.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I have visited the older blocks and the improved block myself and experienced the changes brought about by these works.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I think Members will agree with me that our proposed works will be a marked improvement to the living environment of the rental blocks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will extend these works to more rental blocks and will provide details in due course.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: As some tenants may need to move for the improvement works, HDB will help them to move within the same or nearby blocks.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB will work closely with local organisations and the relevant agencies to ensure a smooth transition.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: (In English): Mr Louis Ng and Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked whether we can better support divorcees in their housing transition, especially those with children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked whether we can help young single unwed parents to rent a flat from HDB more expeditiously.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Last year, we lifted the time bar on divorcees to facilitate their housing transition after divorce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: However, some still face difficulties due to acrimony between both parties.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Some cannot take action on their matrimonial flat because their ex-spouses are uncooperative and do not adhere to the Court Order.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Parties whose ex-spouses are uncooperative may seek legal help to resolve the issue, for example, by applying to the relevant Court to vary the Court Order to empower the Registrar to sign on behalf of the uncooperative party.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are also those awaiting their Final Judgment of divorce.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They may be worried about their next housing arrangement and hoping to apply for a flat earlier.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They will just need to obtain the Final Judgment before collecting their keys and ensure that they are still eligible for the flat that they have booked.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We hope this will give divorcing parties some peace of mind as they go through an emotionally difficult period.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: A final group, as Mr Louis Ng mentioned, are those with shared care and control of their children, who require agreement from their ex-spouse to buy a subsidised flat with their children listed.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In such cases, both parents have a shared and equal right to list their children in their flat.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why we start by encouraging parents to agree on the listings in the best interests of their children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But we understand that there may be difficulties sometimes, So, if there are, indeed, difficulties, HDB will look at the case more closely, and will be prepared to exercise flexibility to help protect the interests of the children.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: HDB will first seek to understand their circumstances to see how best to help them, because their needs differ, and often the input of social workers is also required.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We want to provide help and will do our best to accommodate their requests for housing, be it to purchase a flat or to rent one.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These are just some examples of how HDB does consider individual circumstances which our housing policies may not cater to fully.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This includes households above the public rental income ceiling, which Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap spoke about.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The income ceiling, while relevant, is not the only factor considered.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng asked how the Agri-Food and Veterinary Authority (AVA) addresses cat abandonment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: AVA takes animal abandonment very seriously and will investigate all related feedback.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: To establish the owner of an abandoned pet, AVA gathers evidence by walking the ground, interviewing witnesses and reviewing closed-circuit television footage.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Nonetheless, we recognise the importance of strengthening upstream controls to deter pet abandonment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Under this pilot, CWS has been working with the community on microchipping pet cats to strengthen owner accountability.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We can consider further expansion when the Chong Pang pilot meets these outcomes and when there is strong community support in other parts of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked for an update on the Trap-Neuter-Release-Manage (TNRM) programme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Developed in consultation with Animal Welfare Groups (AWGs) and veterinarians, TNRM is a humane way to sustainably manage the stray dog population nationwide.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Participating AWGs have been able to tap on the Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals' (SPCA's) sterilisation clinic since February.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: In the coming months, AVA and SPCA will also set up a central pool of professional trappers to support the programme.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: AVA has concurrently been engaging stakeholders, such as the Town Councils, People's Association and grassroots organisations, to raise awareness of TNRM and to address any concerns that may arise.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Chairman, we are commemorating the bicentennial this year because the arrival of the British marked the major turning point in our history.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The British also put in place our first town plans.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They provided some basis to guide our urban development.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we have been updating these plans over the years to guide our development.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Each time, it gets more comprehensive in order to meet our growing needs and now, we have even started planning for underground spaces.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our ability to do such detailed long-term planning is a major asset which few other countries or cities are able to do.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is why, every year, we host thousands of visitors at the Singapore City Gallery in the URA building because they are keen to come and learn from us.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond planning, implementation is also important and that is why we are doing more to coordinate the implementation of new infrastructure, especially transport infrastructure, which takes time to build.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that is something which Mr Png Eng Huat highlighted earlier.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we have good planning, long-term planning, and with effective implementation, we can continue to build a better city for Singaporeans, both now and in the future.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Meanwhile, we are working hard to address several more immediate concerns.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, I will focus on three key priorities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, we will keep public housing affordable and accessible.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Getting a home to settle down and start a family is a key milestone for many young couples.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These aspirations are shared by couples all over the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in many other cities, they face big obstacles.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One couple in their late 20s wanted to purchase a home but could not find something suitable within their budget.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Private apartments are too expensive, and public housing options are limited.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For every subsidised flat that is put out, there are close to 60 applicants vying for it.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is double the price of a 3-room flat in Singapore which is also larger in size.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Flats in Singapore are larger in size and much cheaper.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Not to mention that our application rates are also far lower.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Housing is a major challenge in Hong Kong.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And it is so in virtually all cities around the world.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in Singapore, young couples can realise their dreams of owning their own homes.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Of course, from time to time, you would hear comments where people say "Don't compare to other cities.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: How about the price of HDB flats today compared with that in the 1970s and 1980s?

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Why is it so much more expensive today, compared to in the past?" But remember, incomes have also risen considerably over this period.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we really have to look at a broader range of affordability indicators, not just a headline price.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Png Eng Huat highlighted the example of someone who had applied six times but was still unable to get the flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I am sure for such cases, because I have seen some of them myself, they would have applied for BTO flats in mature estates or balance flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I cannot stop people from trying these flats, that is, balance flats or flats in mature estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But given the limited supply of these flats, and the limited space we have in these areas, we really cannot meet all of the demand.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, those who wish to try for a balance flat or a flat in a mature estate, will have to try their luck and hope for the best in the ballot.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But if they go for a BTO flat in a non-mature estate, all of them are able to get it within two to three tries.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is significantly below what it used to be in the past.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I asked my parents who bought their HDB flat in the 1970s.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They said that, indeed, at that time, when they bought their first HDB flat, it was about $25,000, which was about the price in the 1970s.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But at that time, their combined income was less than a thousand dollars per month, just a few hundred dollars, and they had to fork out almost 50% of their income every month for mortgage servicing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, the mortgage servicing ratio is less than 25%, below what it used to be in the past, and it is also well within international benchmarks of affordability.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Internationally, when they look at housing affordability, they would typically look at the servicing ratio of around 30% to 35%.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we are keeping well below that, not to mention that the vast majority of these first-timers are able to service their loans entirely with their Central Provident Fund (CPF), that means, with zero cash.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And even for those who use cash, the amount is very little.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, these are indicators which we track and our commitment is to ensure that HDB flats remain accessible and affordable for all young Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As highlighted by Mr Alex Yam, we will continue to provide affordable housing options for different flat buyer profiles as well.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have flats of different sizes for first-timer and second-timer families and also 2-room flexi flats for singles and the elderly.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We monitor the application rates closely to ensure sufficient supply.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The application rates for singles are still high, as Er Dr Lee Bee Wah mentioned.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But I would assure the Member that we are trying our best, and they have come down.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we are determined to continue to bring it down and we will build more 2-room units to meet the demand.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are also very mindful of the needs of our vulnerable families, including divorcees and single parents, and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling has just shared how we will continue to help them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In short, we will strive to meet the housing needs of Singaporeans in different life stages.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will ensure that no Singaporean is left without adequate housing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For first-timer couples, applying for a BTO flat is a major decision.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One consideration is the location of the flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Very often, potential buyers want to know the planned locations of future BTO sales exercises, not just the present one, so that they can decide whether to put in an application now or hold back and wait for a subsequent sales exercise.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have been careful about revealing too much information on future sales, not because we want to withhold the information but because there will always be unexpected changes to building plans, for example, due to changes in market conditions or demand.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But I understand why buyers would like more information to plan ahead.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will now share upcoming BTO projects half a year in advance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This means that for the upcoming BTO exercise in May, we will share the list of BTO sites for both the August and November 2019 launches.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I hope this change will help flat buyers make more informed choices on their application.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have also been studying ways to improve our BTO application processes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will take effect from the May 2019 BTO exercise onwards.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked for more support for first-timers to live near their parents, and also for families with children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are, indeed, groups that we look out for.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, HDB will continue to offer more 3Gen flats to facilitate intergenerational living.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We also offer various priority schemes, like the Married Child Priority Scheme, Multi-Generation Priority Scheme, Parenthood Priority Scheme for first-timer parents, and Third Child Priority Scheme, a long list of priorities targeted at the groups that Mr Gan Thiam Poh mentioned.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Based on our experience so far, applicants on these priority schemes generally have a good success rate.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Last year, we launched the first batch of shorter waiting time flats, where the waiting time is reduced to two to three years by bringing forward the construction timeline.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh also asked if we can do more.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I have explained, there will be a limit to how many such flats we can offer due to factors like site availability.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But we will continue to review how much more we can do and whether we can compress the timeline further.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Those who need flats more urgently can go for the Sale of Balance Flats (SBF) or the Re-offer of Balance Flats (ROF).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, SBF and now we have ROF, where the flats that were not taken up under SBF goes into the ROF pool.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will help buyers with urgent housing needs to secure a flat quickly because they do not have to wait for the next sales exercise, and the ROF pool will be there for them anytime of the year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But as Mr Alex Yam cautioned, we have to also make sure that the process is fair for everyone.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are starting with a small number of ROF flats in this open pool.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will study the effectiveness and response to this new option and continue thereafter to improve HDB’s sales processes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Of course, besides buying new flats from HDB, there are also many options from the resale market.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As he rightly noted, we cannot simply meet demand through new BTO flats entirely because there may be a risk of over-supply of such new flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we always have to find the right balance between new flats and the resale market.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we have been enhancing the grants for resale flats significantly over the recent years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have enhanced the CPF Housing Grant for first-timers, the Proximity Housing Grant for those who live near or with their parents.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These grants could help subsidise almost half the price of their flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One couple who chose to purchase a resale flat and benefited from these grant enhancements are Mr Sean Morier and Ms Shannon Tan.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They purchased a 5-room resale flat in Simei last year to live together with Shannon's father, Mr Tan Choong Ngiak.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, they benefited from both the CPF Housing Grant and the Proximity Housing Grant, totalling about $70,000, a significant help for their purchase.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As Members can see, the couple have five children, including a recent addition to the family.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is a big family and I am glad they also have a bigger home now to raise their family and to have closer intergenerational family bonding.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With the enhanced grants, resale flats have become more attractive, and there are 5% more transactions in 2018 than the year before.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To give an illustration, five years ago, one in 10 first-timer families bought a resale flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, about one in four first-timer families buy a resale flat because the grants have been enhanced and people can see that between BTO and resale, many still want BTO, but resale is quite an attractive option now with the enhanced grants.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will continue to monitor the market closely and review the quantum of grants to ensure this right balance between BTO supply and resale flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Overall, our priority here is to ensure that HDB flats remain affordable and accessible for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our next priority is to support lower-income and vulnerable families, particularly those who are in public rental housing today.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members have asked if MND can do more to help these families own their own homes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have been and will continue to do so because we believe that home ownership remains central in providing stability and progress for families.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary has shared several initiatives that we are doing, including the setting up of the Home ownership Support Team and the changes to the Fresh Start Housing Scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even with these changes, Fresh Start remains a targeted scheme for a select group of families with young children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are others in rental flats who do not qualify for Fresh Start but would still benefit from some help to purchase their own homes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will extend the grant to those who can benefit from it and are ready to purchase their own homes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also broaden the scope of the grant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Currently, it is limited to 3-room new flats in non-mature estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But some households may prefer to purchase a resale flat, as we just discussed.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will allow the SUHG to be used when households upgrade to 2-room or 3-room flats in non-mature estates, be it new or resale.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is really an expansion of the grant in terms of the people who can apply for it as well as extending the scope of the grant to resale flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The expansion of SUHG is part of our broader efforts to help our rental families progress.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As Members heard just now, the number of public rental households progressing to home ownership has almost doubled over the last five years from 700 to 1,300.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With the above measures, we will try our best to help more public rental households achieve their aspirations of home ownership.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even as we do more on this front, we will also take care of those who continue to live in public rental flats and ensure they have a good living environment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As several Members highlighted yesterday, new rental blocks are better designed and also better integrated with the rest of the precinct.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Now, we even have sold and rental flats within the same block, and on the same floor.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But this is not the case for the older rental blocks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some of these blocks were built 40 or 50 years ago to meet the housing needs of the post-war population, and there is a need for redevelopment of these rental blocks together with the rest of our housing stock.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: With redevelopment, we can move some of the tenants in the older rental blocks to newer flats where they can enjoy a better living environment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Relocation is not easy, especially for the elderly and those with young children.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB will work closely with partners, including local service providers, to ensure a smooth handover of services provided for the tenants.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will provide details on the selected sites when we are ready.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Meanwhile, as the Senior Parliamentary Secretary shared just now, we will continue to maintain and improve our existing rental flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is something which Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Miss Cheryl Chan also highlighted.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Sometimes we have this misperception that rental flats are not eligible for upgrading, unlike sold flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As the Senior Parliamentary Secretary shared just now, for some of the older blocks, we will do more to improve the ventilation and lighting along the corridors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond looking at the designs of the blocks, we will also improve the design of the flat itself to better meet the needs of tenants.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singles in public rental flats currently share a 1-room rental flat under the Joint Singles Scheme (JSS).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we have tried out partitions in some of these new rental flats to create separate sleeping areas for each tenant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our third priority area is to better meet the needs of our elderly, especially with the rapidly ageing population in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Alex Yam asked about the monetisation and housing options available for seniors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One scheme, of course, is the Lease Buyback Scheme (LBS).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Earlier this year, we extended the LBS to 5-room and larger flats, and the response has been positive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In January and February alone, just within these two months, some 160 households from 5-room and larger flats have applied for LBS.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And I agree with Mr Alex Yam that we have to do more to raise awareness of this scheme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is why my MND colleagues and I, over the past few months, have been going around, constituency by constituency, reaching out to grassroots leaders and residents to explain to them what are the schemes available.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: More seniors are aware of LBS and various monetisation options today, but we will continue to do more to raise public awareness.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One couple who have applied for LBS is Mr Mohamed Salleh and Mdm Normah.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They opted for LBS for their 4-room flat, as they wanted to retain their flat to host their four children and 11 grandchildren when they visit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They prefer to keep their flat rather than move to a 2-room flexi.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On top of that, they received their LBS bonus and cash proceeds of $110,000.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is an effective way for those who wish to monetise and unlock the value of their flats for retirement.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: LBS is available for all elderly HDB flat owners.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We understand that LBS may not be an option suitable for everyone.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some may wish to right-size and move to a 2-room flexi flat and so the options are available.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked if MND can facilitate the sale of flats if seniors face difficulties, be it due to market sentiments or the Ethnic Integration Policy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have discussed this before in this House, we recognise the concerns and HDB will continue to do its best to assist them, including by deferring key collection and giving them more time to sell.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One issue with regard to the purchase of older HDB flats is CPF rules, specifically the restriction in CPF usage for flats with less than 60 years of lease remaining.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Some banks also take reference from these CPF restrictions when assessing how much loan to extend.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As a result, both the CPF and loan quantums may be reduced for the purchase of such flats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The CPF rule is intended to safeguard the retirement adequacy of buyers who purchase older flats, but its design has led to some unintended consequences.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, if a buyer would like to buy a 39-year-old flat, they can use full CPF, but one year later, because you hit this "less than 60" years requirement, the amount of CPF will be restricted.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is no good reason why this should be so just because the flat became one year older.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: MND and the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) have been studying the issue.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In fact, the focus should not be on the remaining lease of the flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: What we want to ensure is that buyers purchase flats with leases that are long enough to last them for life.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I have explained the thinking behind how we intend to change the CPF restriction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As seniors right-size, we will provide more housing options for them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are 2-room flexi flats with shorter leases which have proven to be very popular among seniors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As far as possible, we are building these flats with convenient access to amenities, for example, in Kampung Admiralty.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh, Mr Gan Thiam Poh and Mr Murali Pillai also noted that some seniors are looking for alternative residential options like assisted living.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Senior Minister of State Amy Khor shared about this yesterday.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, that is why MND and the Ministry of Health must come together to offer assisted living.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not something that one Ministry can do.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When you go for assisted living, you are not just buying a flat, but a package of care services tied to the assisted living flat.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is not just the hardware, it is the flat plus the services combined as one package.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Typically, in such assisted living apartments, there will be more communal and shared spaces for residents to interact with one another, there will be services that are part of the package and the individual living units will be a bit smaller.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is a typical typology of an assisted living apartment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As the assisted living model is new, we will conduct focus group discussions to seek views on the proposed concept for assisted living in public housing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The key here is that, when we put out these sites for private developers or private players to bid, we do not want it to be simply a property play.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are working on them and will provide details when we are ready.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides the three priority areas I have just outlined, many Members highlighted the importance of ensuring that our homes and estates remain liveable and vibrant, and I fully agree with them.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB takes its role as master developer and planner very seriously.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For new towns, much effort goes behind the scenes in planning and developing our estates and ensuring the town has a full range of amenities and facilities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And HDB is always looking to improve, taking in feedback, suggestions and how the next project can be done better.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, I visited Punggol recently where we opened the new neighbourhood centre at Oasis Terraces.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is a prime site where the neighbourhood centre is located.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is waterfront site, next to a Light Rail Transit station.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We could have sold this to a private developer, but we decided that it is central to the neighbourhood, we want to make it an HDB neighbourhood centre.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, HDB develops it as a neighbourhood centre with integrated facilities, rooftop gardens, greenery, play areas and lots of common spaces for residents to interact with one another.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: If you get feedback and responses from the residents, it has certainly been very positive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
