text: So, this is the first of our new generation neighbourhood centres and we will be doing more in the coming years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For our older towns, we have various upgrading plans in place.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: At the flat and precinct level, we have the Home Improvement Programme (HIP) and the Neighbourhood Renewal Programme.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Png Eng Huat highlighted some issues with the quality of HIP workmanship and some projects as well as the issue of clothes drying rack on the lower floors.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will look at these specifically on these particular issues.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah offered several suggestions, such as using Community Improvement Projects Committee (CIPC) funds for designated smoking points, smoke-free flats and Temporary Occupation Licence charges for essential services.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Again, these are all suggestions we will look into.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Png Eng Huat asked about lift access for blocks without LUP.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I think the Member and several Members have asked this question before.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are continuing to explore technical solutions for the remaining blocks where lift upgrading is not viable today.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Meanwhile, we have explained in this House that for those who are in urgent need of direct lift access due to medical conditions or disability, they may approach HDB for assistance.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Not completed construction, because that will take a while, but we will have announcements by end of this year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, the big question is: what about HIP for the blocks built between 1987 and 1997?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It does not mean that everything will be completed next year.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will have to be done in phases over a period of time, but we will commence the process from next year onwards.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Beyond upgrading, we are looking at VERS and longer-term plans to systematically redevelop and rejuvenate our older HDB towns.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As Mr Chong Kee Hiong said, this ought to be done not just at the individual block but also at the precinct level.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are planning well in advance for this because we do not want public housing in Singapore to degenerate into urban slums like what has happened in other cities.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Public housing must continue to integrate Singaporeans of all backgrounds.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We must never become segregated by class, race or income.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This also relates to the point made by Assoc Prof Walter Theseira about the differences in the prices of HDB flats across the island and whether this would lead to more social stratification.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is something we are aware of and are continuing to watch out for, including looking at different ways in which we can mitigate against this.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the longer term, the best way to tackle this is to ensure that every part of Singapore is well developed, and that every HDB precinct has good amenities and facilities, convenient access to the transport network as well as job centres closer to home.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is what we have been doing and the upcoming Masterplan will continue with more efforts in this direction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It does not mean that we can automatically equalise property values.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But at least we can temper some of the excesses in the market.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I should also say, when you speak to Singaporeans, you find that they have an attachment to a particular place and it often goes beyond monetary value.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I grew up in the East, and my friends and neighbours will always say the East is special, we will never move.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Indeed, many of them still stay there, their children are still staying there.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When I joined politics in 2011 and served in Boon Lay in the west, many residents in the west have a close affinity for the area and have many special memories growing up there.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Now, I am a Member of Parliament in Marsiling-Yew Tee, in the north.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: My residents are proud to be in the north.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: They call Woodlands the star destination and I have come to grow fond of the area, too.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Are there price differences in flat values between the different parts of Singapore?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But the residents in each area take great pride in where they stay.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is about the memories they have of the place, the sense of community, the connection and identity with where they grew up, and you cannot attach a price tag to these.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we have to continue working hard to make sure that every HDB town, every precinct, is kept liveable and vibrant, both now and in the future.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Besides upgrading our housing estates, we will also remake our city.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Every major city in the world is constantly inventing and reinventing itself.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is the only way for cities to survive and thrive.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Indeed, throughout history, cities have risen and fallen.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Detroit was once the envy of the world, one of the most prosperous cities in the United States (US), they call it the Paris of the West, and then it went into decline and became bankrupt.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Today, we enjoy high international standing as a modern liveable city, a beautiful city in a garden.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But what we have today can be easily replicated in other cities, and they can very likely do it better as they have more space and more natural endowments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As we remake our city, we must also prepare ahead for new challenges and threats.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The world is warming up, and it is happening sooner and more rapidly than people had expected.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we are redoubling our efforts to make Singapore one of the greenest cities in the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Several Members have raised this, and I am glad they did because it is a critical part of our development plans.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: When we say we are not done building Singapore, we are not just referring to more buildings and physical infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A major part of this effort is to actively green Singapore for future generations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That means conserving and enhancing existing greenery, as well as safeguarding spaces for greenery even as we continue to develop.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: A greener Singapore will, in turn, help to mitigate extreme temperatures and provide a natural respite from traffic, noise and congestion.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The entire Rail Corridor is 24 kilometres (km) long.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, you can run up and down and do more than a marathon.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are embracing green in the broader sense, not just biodiversity and greenery, but also advanced clean-tech solutions, be it solar panels, electric buses, autonomous shuttles, zero-energy buildings or district cooling systems.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are testing out sustainable technologies at both the building and the district levels.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are all examples of what we are doing to be a leading sustainable city.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we are also investing in research and development in a whole range of urban solutions, from building materials to smart sensors to underground space.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, we are trying out coatings or construction materials that absorb less heat and that can help lower the ambient temperature.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And once proven to be technically feasible and cost-effective, we will look into implementation of these and other technologies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our next phase of development cannot just be a continuation of business-as-usual practices.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will set higher eco-friendly standards and new urban practices for sustainable living.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is also how we can stay relevant and useful to many other cities around the world, all of which are grappling with similar issues.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Even as we do all this, we recognise that tackling climate change requires a concerted global response, and there is no certainty how this will evolve in the years to come.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Of course, there are many uncertainties surrounding these projections.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But I would say there are more downside risks than upside.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, if the Antarctic ice sheet melts faster than expected, the sea level would rise dramatically and it may well happen earlier, causing significant global impact by 2050, and that is just 30 years from now.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Imagine what this means for our little red dot which is low-lying and surrounded by water.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, climate change is not a remote issue.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: That is why we have been carefully studying the risks and impact of sea level rise and looking at detailed measures to protect our coastal areas.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Major investments will be needed in the form of reclamation, sea walls or pumping stations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Many of them are living below sea level today in Rotterdam and we are learning from their experience with our polder project in Pulau Tekong.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Remaking our city is not just about preparing for challenges.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are also many exciting opportunities ahead and we have plans to make Singapore stand out as a leading city for Asia and the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We are planning for three major gateways in the East, West and North.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These key developments will help support our growth and create more jobs across the island.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, there will be more opportunities for Singaporeans to live and work closer to their homes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Of course, we also have to focus on the centre.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have plans for the East, West and North, but the centre and the South cannot be neglected.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This has historically been at the heart of economic, civic and cultural activities, and we will ensure it remains attractive and vibrant.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have just revealed exciting plans for Orchard Road.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want it to be more than just a shopping destination.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There are different precincts along the 2.4-km stretch of Orchard Road offering more diverse and vibrant lifestyle destinations so that we can make Orchard Road one of the great streets of the world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Nearby, we have the Civic District, Fort Canning Park, Bras Basah and Bugis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We can connect all of these together to create an expanded arts, cultural and heritage precinct.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Within the city, the core area is the Central Business District (CBD).

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Downtown CBD – Raffles Place, Tanjong Pagar/Maxwell, Robinson/Shenton – is largely dominated by older office developments, single-use offices, quite unlike the Marina Bay CBD extension which was planned as a mixed-use district.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Most of the buildings in the CBD are privately owned.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have an existing scheme to allow intensification of commercial buildings through bonus plot ratios.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Most eligible buildings have already made use of this to maximise their development.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, it is timely for us to review.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will explore new incentives to better support rejuvenation in CBD.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Specifically, we want to encourage more mixed uses in CBD, such as residential and hotel, so that there will be activities beyond office hours.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This will also better optimise and intensify the use of prime CBD land.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Then we can make our CBD not just a place to work, but also an attractive and vibrant place to live and play.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our plans are not just confined to the main island we live in.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore is made up of more than 60 offshore islands.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have major development plans for Sentosa and Brani to offer new attractions for tourists and Singaporeans alike.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have started reclamation work in Pulau Tekong for military training.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will also carry out improvement works on Pedra Branca.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These works will enhance maritime safety and security in the area, and provide more rapid response for search and rescue.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the longer term, we have two major sites for future redevelopment.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: These are at Paya Lebar and the Greater Southern Waterfront.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It is a new area, bigger than the size of Ang Mo Kio Town, for both public and private housing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In addition, there are non-port areas like the Pasir Panjang Power District, Keppel Club and Sentosa, which contribute another 1,000 ha.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For example, in Pasir Panjang, we will push the existing substation there underground.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Singapore Power (SP) is working on this and it will be the largest underground substation in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will repurpose the former power station buildings and open up the area to the public.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will enhance green spaces in Mount Faber and develop the Pasir Panjang Linear Park.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And in the area where Keppel Club is today, we will develop new housing and residential options after the land is returned to the Government.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over time, we will redevelop and stitch together the entire waterfront from Pasir Panjang to Marina East.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: It will be an exciting new waterfront development with green and blue spaces for all to enjoy.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Over the last 50 years, Singapore has transformed way beyond what anyone could have imagined.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our homes, transformed from kampongs to beautiful high-rise buildings with sky gardens, surrounded by playgrounds and parks.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our city, transformed from overcrowded slums to a green and vibrant metropolis.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: To our founding Prime Minister Mr Lee Kuan Yew, this transformation from mudflat to metropolis was a unique opportunity.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As he put it in an interview with the Centre for Liveable Cities, “I’m pleased that we redeveloped the city when there was a chance to do it… ...That was a chance of a lifetime”.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But now, we have the chance of our lifetime to reimagine and to remake our city.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is much more than just having bigger and taller buildings.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As Mr Lee once said, Singapore is more than just a place on the map.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Our city must reflect who we are as a people – our spirit and our values.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want to make Singapore an outstanding place where all can strive for a better life even in an uncertain and volatile world.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We want to create new versions of urban living, each more fulfilling and sustainable, more beautiful and fun than the previous one.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is where the human spirit will flourish and inspire.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we invite all Singaporeans to join us in this exciting journey.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: There is much more we can achieve together.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Chairman, I have three clarifications for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The first is that in my speech last night, I asked for some details of the Home ownership Support Team.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What are the criteria that they will be considering and what is their ambit and how many rental households could potentially move towards home ownership in the next five years?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The second clarification relates to what the Senior Parliamentary Secretary shared earlier on the Fresh Start Housing Scheme.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: In terms of the new Fresh Start Support Programme (FSSP) and the appointment of a new service provider, how would this differ from the existing work that our Family Service Centres (FSCs) are doing on the ground because the numbers are relatively small?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I note that there are some differences between those who are emplaced and those who successfully apply for a flat.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What has been the main barrier to those who are emplaced but do not qualify thereafter?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: With regard to the difference between FSSP and FSCs, the new FSSP will focus on supporting the families to stay on track for a fresh start towards home ownership.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For example, they will look at how they can help them ensure that they have enough housing budget to be able to afford the flat.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: For FSCs, they look at how to ensure family stability for the family unit.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But for the purposes of ensuring that the family successfully gets on to home ownership, FSSP will work together with the FSC to achieve that purpose.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Mr Alex Yam, you had a question about the numbers for FSSP?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Numbers in terms of what is the main barrier to those who are emplaced but do not qualify.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Many of the rental families have very unique situations that they sometimes have to overcome.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: It could be issues, such as income stability, they may be facing challenges in terms of medical or social conditions.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: These are the various areas that FSSP will work with the families to help them overcome.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: In terms of the Home ownership Support Team?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Sorry, could I ask you to repeat the question?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Last night, I mentioned that I welcomed the announcement of the Home Ownership Support Team.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They will look at whether the families are stable, whether they have income stability, that they do not have family conflict and, if they have some of these challenges, how they can work with them towards home ownership.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First, I would like to thank Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling for sharing about the support for divorcees.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But there are some who are stuck in their housing transition.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I met a resident whose divorce was finalised and the Court ordered for the flat to be sold.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It has been a few years, but the flat is still unsold because her ex-husband refuses to open the door for viewings.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And she cannot buy her next home because she is listed as an owner of the flat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: She also needs the proceeds from the sale to buy her next flat.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, my question is: is there anything that HDB can do to move along the sale of the flat so that she and her children can move on with their lives?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And my next question is for Minister Desmond Lee.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Yesterday, the Minister answered about this heavy vehicle park.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is, indeed, a big problem faced by many residents in Yishun New Town.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: There are three or four lane roads there, which are, at night, so empty.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, can we make use of some of those roads to have the season heavy vehicle parking?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Indeed, it is a difficult situation, the example that she cited.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And for the instance the Member mentioned about viewing times, timeline for the sale of the flat, the resident can also seek legal help and have that included in the Court Order as well.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But I guess the starting point is that her resident would have to consult a lawyer and have the Court Order varied.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: For cases that have been concluded many years ago, how does one go about getting the Court Order?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: In fact, this is not only one case because, recently, I have come across quite a number of similar cases where the ex-spouse and the parents still continue to live inside and refuse to let the potential buyers view the flats.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Yes, it is possible to still bring a case against the uncooperative party.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: And I would like to add that if the party refuses to cooperate, you can bring up a case for contempt of the Court and he can actually be penalised for it.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Chairman, we are mindful of the local needs for heavy vehicle parking.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: At the national level, there are more than adequate heavy vehicle lots, but we are quite mindful that at the local level, there may be certain needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: My colleagues from URA and the Land Transport Authority (LTA) have been working with colleagues where there are specific pain points.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Mr Chairman, I have a clarification for the Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I welcome MND's move to explore provision for rest areas under the new planning parameters.

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: However, would MND review its current policy to consider rest areas included under the item not counted under gross floor area so that it will be excluded from a Development Charge (DC)?

speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This would incentivise existing building owners to carve out rest areas for the workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Chairman, I thank the Member for taking a keen interest in the welfare of our cleaners and the other low-wage workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Let us look at what we have today.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Because DC will only apply in cases where the proposal would result in an enhancement of the value of land.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: So, if there is no enhancement of value, then, it is not applicable.

speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: But rest assured that MND and MOM are both looking into this and will see how we can do better to promote rest areas in buildings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, I agree with the Minister that all HDB estates are and must continue to be good towns that are special to our hearts, regardless of price differences.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: There are a number of older flats, rental and public, in the central region.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: These sites are getting on in years and will have to be redeveloped at some point.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: If so, what can be done to ensure that such flats continue to reflect the broad majority of Singaporeans, the heart of Singapore, rather than just the elite?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Assoc Prof Theseira highlighted a concern about pricing.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And as he said in his cut earlier, it is very difficult to get this balance right because if you price it to market, then only the very well-off can afford.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the other hand, if you want to make it affordable, then the only way is through a big discount to the BTO price but that leads to a lottery effect and the lucky guy who gets the flat get a so-called "windfall", compared to others who buy flats elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And that is not a fair distribution of housing subsidies.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Assoc Prof Theseira did talk about various options to try and think about different ways of selling HDB flats in these central locations.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I will take on board these suggestions and we will continue to study what is the best way forward.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, I am heartened to note from the hon Minister's speech that young couples applying for BTO flats in non-mature estates will be able to secure their flats within two to three bids.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I have a query in relation to young couples whose combined incomes breach the income ceiling.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I understand that the policy objective behind the income ceiling is to husband the housing subsidies such that we direct it to those who need it the most.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: However, in relation to young couples whose incomes breach the income ceiling, they may not necessarily have an option to purchase a condominium because condominium prices have increased quite significantly as well.

speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
text: I welcome the hon Minister's comments on this, please.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will continue to see how it can be updated as incomes grow so that more Singaporeans can benefit.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: In the meantime, for those who exceed the HDB income ceiling, there are options like the Executive Condominiums (ECs) which they can apply for as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This first one is to Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I am glad to know about Home ownership Support Team.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: She mentioned it repeatedly, today and before this as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: But she mentioned about income stability just now, in terms of criteria.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Most of the applicants need to have 12 months of continuous employment.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In most cases where I have seen residents come to me is when they have difficulty in meeting that 12-month continuous employment, particularly because they are working part-time, or they are in between jobs, or they are either gig workers or temporary workers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, in such situations, can HDB, on top of giving the usual answer where they will be flexible in such circumstances, whether they can review such cases for the Home ownership Support Team cases in the future?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It is very apt that the Minister highlighted about the rising seawater levels as an important issue, going forward.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Can the Minister share with us whether there is a timeline when the Government will actually share with the public or Parliament the impact of the seawater level rising on housing in general, in Singapore in general and also in terms of budget expenditure, maybe in the future?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: It would be useful because it is a particularly important concern for Singapore in the long run.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On calculating the income, I just would like to share that income from odd jobs is counted when we look at income stability for the applicant.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We do not just look at Home ownership Support Team separately from FSSP.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Basically, we want to work with the applicants if they demonstrate that they are very keen to get on to home ownership.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, where there are specific criteria that they face difficulty meeting the Home ownership Support Team or the FSSP, depending on which programme that he can get on, they will work actively with the applicant to try to help him meet the criterion which he finds challenging at that point in time.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, the short answer to the question is yes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: This is certainly an important issue which we will share with Singaporeans when ready.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: As I mentioned, we are now doing very detailed studies around the coastal areas in Singapore, that is, which are the more vulnerable areas, how will rising sea levels impact these coastal areas and beyond within Singapore itself.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And then, on top of that, what are the appropriate protective measures to take?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And there are a range of different measures that are necessary and all of these will require major investments.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have time to do it, but we are planning well ahead.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: And when we are ready, we will certainly share this information with Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: Mr Chairman, just some questions for the Senior Parliamentary Secretary.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I am glad to hear of the improvements to the older rental flats.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: I just want to ask Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling how many blocks will be expected to benefit from these improvements and whether she can share the likely localities for improvements.

speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
text: And what is the indicative timeline for HDB to start work?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: Like I mentioned, the improvement works are specifically to assist with lighting as well as for ventilation.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, the rental blocks are dispersed across the whole of Singapore.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: There are some specific areas where rental blocks in the 1960s and 1970s are congregated.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will be identifying the blocks and we will release more details in due course.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Chairman, Minister Desmond Lee mentioned last night that we are reviewing the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) framework in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I think that was already mentioned in June 2017, if I am not wrong.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I am just wondering whether there is a timeframe for this review and when do we expect to complete it.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: For Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling, I thank her for mentioning that we are going to review pet ownership in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But could I just ask very specifically whether MND is reviewing the possibility of microchipping and licensing pet cats in Singapore so that we can deter pet cat abandonment?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Second, with regard to the single unweds, I am very thankful that the Senior Parliamentary Secretary has said that HDB will accept the application for HDB flats at the HDB counters.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: But I do understand this is still subject to a case-by-case review.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: The review that AVA will be embarking on, as I mentioned, is to look at how we can promote more responsible pet ownership, as well as deter abandonment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, we will look at a variety of measures.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: We will also be looking into the additional measures that the Member talked about.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: This will be part of our entire holistic review of what is the best regulatory approach to deter pet abandonment.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: I would just like to add that it is very important that the education part of it goes upstream and work with the community and pet owners to encourage them to be responsible pet owners.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is going to be very important because when you look at regulations, we have to balance the needs of various stakeholders.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: On the Member's question about single unwed parents, they can face unique family situations.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: When we consider their need for housing, we will look specifically into the background, whether or not they have family support and their income levels.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: They may face a variety of issues at home.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That is why whenever we consider the situation for single unwed parents, we also seek inputs from social service workers.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: So, I would just like to assure the Member that we take a very holistic approach.

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: If that is the case, why is it that the CPF housing grant for first-timers buying resale flats is smaller for couples buying bigger BTO flats?

speaker: Mr Yee Chia Hsing (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I would also like to highlight that before the increase in 2017, the amount of CPF housing grant is flat, regardless of the size of the resale flat that these couples are buying.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we have increased for both, but we have tiered it compared to the past.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Having that progressivity in the grants can be helpful, given the considerations that we have in wanting to address some of the concerns about social inequality that we face in society.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, the tiering of the grant was a move in that direction.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: I do not think it will deter those who have the means to buy a bigger flat and, if anything, we want to also send a right signal that home-buyers ought to be prudent and do not overstretch themselves unnecessarily, but buy a flat that is suitable within their means.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The Minister mentioned earlier that there will be more clarity in BTO prices so that applicants could better assess their affordability.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At the time of application of flats, there is also home-loan assessment on how much the applicants could borrow.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, when the time comes for key collection, the applicants may have a lower income because of change of job or because of the environment.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Therefore, they may not be able to afford the same flat.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: At the same time, the grant given to applicants are assessed at the point of application.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, it is sort of a double-whammy: he cannot get a higher grant because he was assessed earlier; and because of his reduced income, his home-loan entitlement has dropped and so he could no longer afford the flat that he applied earlier.

speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Could the Minister explain how HDB could help this group of applicants?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Mr Chairman, we do see some of these cases.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: But from time to time, we do have examples of home buyers who, very unfortunately, during their waiting period, something happens to them before they could collect their keys.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: HDB tries to be as helpful as possible.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: One way is to see how best to support them still with the loan quantum.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: The qualification here is that we do not want, as I said earlier, to end up with them overstretching themselves and their finances.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, we will assess each individual case and see how best to support them, firstly, on the loan.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have a clarification for Minister Desmond Lee.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Could I just clarify with him regarding the lane usage of the park connectors on the point that I raised, which is, the safety of the park connectors?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Specifically, are people allowed to walk on the two lanes with the different markings?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I say this because, if that is the case, then really, I would like the Ministry to consider reviewing the lane markings because it is really unsafe when you have people walking on both sides and the personal mobility device users, the cyclists and other users who have to wade through the traffic, and people are not exactly keeping left.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Keeping left in such a situation may not really be the correct thing to do as well.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, NParks will relook at the way in which we explain the usage of the lanes and the Park Connector Network (PCN) to ensure that both pedestrians and users of bicycles and other mobility devices have a seamless understanding when they move on to PCNs from the shared lanes that are under LTA along our pedestrian walkways.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some, of course, are shared; some are separated.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The clarity needs to go out in terms of public education, also in the signage.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I have just one follow-up question for Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Could I check how long does it usually take HDB to process the application for the single unweds, say, for rental housing?

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: That would depend on the submission of the documents that are required, as well as whether the inputs from the social worker have come in.

speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
text: But in general, if it is an urgent case, and the assessment can be quickly done, the rental application can be processed quite quickly.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Three for Minister Lawrence Wong; and three for Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I am very heartened to hear from the Minister that the building of 2-room flats has been intensified, and the singles do not have to wait for too long to buy their 2-room flats.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The second question is: for HIP2 for flats built in 1987 to 1997 of which the announcement will be made next year, when will be the announcement for the last batch to be made, based on the current plan?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: This is so that residents can know because there is an expectation.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The third question I asked in my speech was: whether the large-scale town-wide funding can also be extended to private estates?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: This is because I find that some of the private estates are really short on amenities, and the best way could be to make use of the large-scale town-wide funding as those areas may not qualify for EUP.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: And I have three questions for Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I am glad to hear about the Inter-Agency Coordinating Committee (IACC).

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Will IACC also look into Temporary Occupation Permit (TOP) and Certificate of Statutory Completion (CSC) processes?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: This is because for some of the projects, the TOP or the CSC have been stuck there for a long time due to certain compliance matters taking a long time and not moving forward.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: On the one hand, the developers are very worried about the quality control imposed and want to apply for TOP.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: On the other hand, there is the compliance issue.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The second question is about awarding contracts to local contractors.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: We are aware that there is a World Trade Organization (WTO) requirement, but I hope that the Minister of State is also aware that some of our local contractors have grown and they are ready to take on big projects like those which are $400 million and above.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: I hope that there are certain ways to see how we can let our bigger contractors have a bigger share of the pie of bigger projects.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: The third question is about services diversion which, very often, take a long time and hence they delay the projects.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Is there any possibility to get whatever service diversions within the land parcel diverted before the land is put up for tender?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: Or can the diversion be concurrently done, because it takes a long time to carry out the diversion subsequently?

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We have already brought it down to an application rate of just above four.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: We will focus on that before we think about any further changes.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, that is how the process will start, and in the year following that we will continue with this process.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: How fast it can be done really depends on fiscal space and the availability of funds.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I really cannot commit to a schedule today, but if you were to look at the previous round when we did the HIP for flats built before 1986, it took more than 10 years to complete.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah has been following and tracking this very carefully, she tells me 13 years.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: So, I think residents must have some context.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: On the large-scale town-wide projects, under the CIPC, they were designed specifically for public housing estates.

speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
text: For private estates, we have EUP, and we are happy to see if more can be done and whether the scope of works in the EUP can be enhanced.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: But I want to stress again that we are also a signatory to the WTO Agreement on Government Procurement.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, we cannot give projects away to locals and favour locals over foreign companies.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Today, we also have local companies which are winning large Government projects.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: To a certain extent, there is opportunity for local firms to win large contracting projects.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our Price Quality Method has also shifted towards focusing more on quality as opposed to cost.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Our local firms need to build up capability to address this portion in terms of quality, track record and experience.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We hope to upskill and build up capabilities for our local firms.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: This is something we will look closely at.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I hope that the local firms can also do their part and build up capabilities to address these opportunities.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Specific to IACC, I am glad that the Member has also noted the changes that we have done to IACC.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: For issues, such as service diversion, TOP and CSC that are delayed, please raise them to the IACC, which will see how best to assist.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Certainly, what we want to try to do is to facilitate and help to bring closure to some of these projects as soon as possible.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Alex Yam, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to thank Minister Lawrence Wong, Minister Grace Fu, Minister Desmond Lee, Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad and Senior Parliamentary Secretary Sun Xueling for listening intently to us and considering seriously our suggestions.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: We do wait eagerly for MND to implement promptly some of these measures.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam
text: Therefore, Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
